//! Bounded, allocation-free ACPI structure validation and MADT parsing.
//!
//! These helpers consume byte slices supplied by a future checked table reader.
//! They do not map or dereference physical addresses and do not initialize APICs.

pub const MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE: usize = 64 * 1024;
const RSDP_V1_SIZE: usize = 20;
const RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE: usize = 36;
const SDT_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 36;
const MADT_FIXED_SIZE: usize = 44;
const MAX_MADT_ENTRIES: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES: usize = 1024;
const MAX_LOCAL_APICS: usize = 16;
const MAX_IO_APICS: usize = 8;
const MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES: usize = 16;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiError {
    StructureTooShort,
    StructureTooLarge,
    InvalidRsdpSignature,
    InvalidRsdpChecksum,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpLength,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum,
    UnsupportedRsdpRevision(u8),
    InvalidSdtLength,
    InvalidSdtChecksum,
    NotRootPointerTable,
    InvalidRootPointerTableLength,
    TooManyRootPointers,
    NullRootPointer,
    NotMadt,
    InvalidMadtLength,
    InvalidMadtEntryLength,
    TooManyMadtEntries,
    MadtCapacityExceeded,
    UnsupportedMadtEntryType(u8),
}

/// Validated root-system-description pointer fields copied out of the ACPI bytes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rsdp {
    pub revision: u8,
    pub rsdt_address: u32,
    pub xsdt_address: Option<u64>,
}

impl Rsdp {
    /// Validate an RSDP byte slice and copy its table addresses.
    ///
    /// ACPI 1.0 (revision 0) structures use the 20-byte legacy checksum. ACPI
    /// 2.0+ structures must include and pass the extended checksum.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V1_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        if bytes[..8] != *b"RSD PTR " {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpSignature);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..RSDP_V1_SIZE]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpChecksum);
        }

        let revision = bytes[15];
        let rsdt_address = read_u32(bytes, 16);
        if revision == 0 {
            return Ok(Self {
                revision,
                rsdt_address,
                xsdt_address: None,
            });
        }
        if revision < 2 {
            return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedRsdpRevision(revision));
        }
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }

        let length = read_u32(bytes, 20) as usize;
        if !(RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE..=MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE).contains(&length) || length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            revision,
            rsdt_address,
            xsdt_address: Some(read_u64(bytes, 24)),
        })
    }
}

/// A system-description table whose advertised length and checksum were checked.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Sdt<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pub signature: [u8; 4],
    pub revision: u8,
}

impl<'a> Sdt<'a> {
    /// Validate an SDT header, bounded length, and checksum.
    ///
    /// Bytes following the advertised table length are ignored. The caller must
    /// still ensure that the complete advertised table is in the supplied slice.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        let length = read_u32(bytes, 4) as usize;
        if length < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if length > MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooLarge);
        }
        if length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            bytes: &bytes[..length],
            signature: [bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]],
            revision: bytes[8],
        })
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len()
    }

    pub fn root_pointer_table(self) -> Result<RootPointerTable<'a>, AcpiError> {
        RootPointerTable::parse(self)
    }
}

/// Bounded, zero-allocation view of an ACPI RSDT or XSDT address array.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RootPointerTable<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    entry_width: usize,
    entry_count: usize,
}

impl<'a> RootPointerTable<'a> {
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'a>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        let entry_width = match table.signature {
            [b'R', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 4,
            [b'X', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 8,
            _ => return Err(AcpiError::NotRootPointerTable),
        };
        let payload_length = table.bytes.len() - SDT_HEADER_SIZE;
        if payload_length % entry_width != 0 {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength);
        }
        let entry_count = payload_length / entry_width;
        if entry_count > MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES {
            return Err(AcpiError::TooManyRootPointers);
        }
        let pointers = &table.bytes[SDT_HEADER_SIZE..];
        for index in 0..entry_count {
            let offset = index * entry_width;
            let address = if entry_width == 4 {
                read_u32(pointers, offset) as u64
            } else {
                read_u64(pointers, offset)
            };
            if address == 0 {
                return Err(AcpiError::NullRootPointer);
            }
        }
        Ok(Self {
            bytes: pointers,
            entry_width,
            entry_count,
        })
    }

    pub const fn is_xsdt(&self) -> bool {
        self.entry_width == 8
    }

    pub const fn entry_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entry_count
    }

    pub fn address_at(&self, index: usize) -> Option<u64> {
        if index >= self.entry_count {
            return None;
        }
        let offset = index.checked_mul(self.entry_width)?;
        Some(if self.entry_width == 4 {
            read_u32(self.bytes, offset) as u64
        } else {
            read_u64(self.bytes, offset)
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LocalApic {
    pub processor_uid: u8,
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub flags: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IoApic {
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub physical_address: u32,
    pub global_system_interrupt_base: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InterruptSourceOverride {
    pub bus: u8,
    pub source: u8,
    pub global_system_interrupt: u32,
    pub flags: u16,
}

/// Fixed-capacity, copied data from an xAPIC-compatible MADT.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Madt {
    pub local_apic_address: u64,
    pub flags: u32,
    local_apics: [Option<LocalApic>; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
    local_apic_count: usize,
    io_apics: [Option<IoApic>; MAX_IO_APICS],
    io_apic_count: usize,
    interrupt_overrides: [Option<InterruptSourceOverride>; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
    interrupt_override_count: usize,
}

impl Madt {
    /// Parse the known xAPIC MADT records into bounded owned arrays.
    ///
    /// Unknown record types are skipped after validating their common header.
    /// x2APIC processor records are rejected because this parser does not yet
    /// establish x2APIC mode or destination-ID policy.
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'_>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if table.signature != *b"APIC" {
            return Err(AcpiError::NotMadt);
        }
        if table.bytes.len() < MADT_FIXED_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtLength);
        }

        let mut madt = Self {
            local_apic_address: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE) as u64,
            flags: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE + 4),
            local_apics: [None; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
            local_apic_count: 0,
            io_apics: [None; MAX_IO_APICS],
            io_apic_count: 0,
            interrupt_overrides: [None; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
            interrupt_override_count: 0,
        };

        let mut offset = MADT_FIXED_SIZE;
        let mut entry_count = 0;
        while offset < table.bytes.len() {
            if table.bytes.len() - offset < 2 {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            let entry_type = table.bytes[offset];
            let entry_length = table.bytes[offset + 1] as usize;
            if entry_length < 2 || entry_length > table.bytes.len() - offset {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            entry_count += 1;
            if entry_count > MAX_MADT_ENTRIES {
                return Err(AcpiError::TooManyMadtEntries);
            }

            let entry = &table.bytes[offset..offset + entry_length];
            match entry_type {
                0 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 8)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.local_apics,
                        &mut madt.local_apic_count,
                        LocalApic {
                            processor_uid: entry[2],
                            apic_id: entry[3],
                            flags: read_u32(entry, 4),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                1 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.io_apics,
                        &mut madt.io_apic_count,
                        IoApic {
                            apic_id: entry[2],
                            physical_address: read_u32(entry, 4),
                            global_system_interrupt_base: read_u32(entry, 8),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                2 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 10)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.interrupt_overrides,
                        &mut madt.interrupt_override_count,
                        InterruptSourceOverride {
                            bus: entry[2],
                            source: entry[3],
                            global_system_interrupt: read_u32(entry, 4),
                            flags: read_u16(entry, 8),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                5 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    madt.local_apic_address = read_u64(entry, 4);
                }
                9 => return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedMadtEntryType(entry_type)),
                _ => {}
            }
            offset += entry_length;
        }

        Ok(madt)
    }

    pub fn local_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = LocalApic> + '_ {
        self.local_apics[..self.local_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn io_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = IoApic> + '_ {
        self.io_apics[..self.io_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn interrupt_overrides(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = InterruptSourceOverride> + '_ {
        self.interrupt_overrides[..self.interrupt_override_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }
}

fn require_entry_length(actual: usize, expected: usize) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    if actual == expected {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength)
    }
}

fn push<T: Copy, const N: usize>(
    entries: &mut [Option<T>; N],
    count: &mut usize,
    value: T,
) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    let Some(slot) = entries.get_mut(*count) else {
        return Err(AcpiError::MadtCapacityExceeded);
    };
    *slot = Some(value);
    *count += 1;
    Ok(())
}

fn checksum_is_valid(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    bytes.iter().fold(0u8, |sum, byte| sum.wrapping_add(*byte)) == 0
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[offset], bytes[offset + 1]])
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
    ])
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
        bytes[offset + 4],
        bytes[offset + 5],
        bytes[offset + 6],
        bytes[offset + 7],
    ])
}

        assert_eq!(madt.flags, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            madt.local_apics().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::LocalApic {
                processor_uid: 1,
                apic_id: 2,
                flags: 1,
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            madt.io_apics().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::IoApic {
                apic_id: 3,
                physical_address: 0xfec0_0000,
                global_system_interrupt_base: 0,
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            madt.interrupt_overrides().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::InterruptSourceOverride {
                bus: 0,
                source: 0,
                global_system_interrupt: 9,
                flags: 0,
            }]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_truncated_and_unsupported_madt_records() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body.extend_from_slice(&[1, 11, 0, 0]);
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength)
        );

        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body.extend_from_slice(&[9, 2]);
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedMadtEntryType(9))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_fixed_madt_capacity_exhaustion() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        for apic_id in 0..17u8 {
            body.extend_from_slice(&[0, 8, apic_id, apic_id, 1, 0, 0, 0]);
        }
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::MadtCapacityExceeded)
        );
    }
}

# ACPI parsing foundation

## Current implementation

`src/acpi.rs` provides allocation-free helpers over caller-supplied byte slices:

- RSDP signature, legacy checksum, revision, bounded extended length, and extended checksum validation.
- System Description Table header, advertised-length, 64 KiB maximum-size, and checksum validation.
- Bounded, allocation-free RSDT/XSDT pointer-array views with width, alignment, null-entry, and count checks.
- Fixed-capacity copying of MADT local-APIC, I/O-APIC, interrupt-source-override, and local-APIC-address-override records.
- Structural rejection of malformed/truncated MADT records, unsupported x2APIC processor records, excessive entry counts, and fixed-array exhaustion.

These functions validate data already present in a byte slice. They neither follow physical addresses nor prove the slice came from ACPI-reclaimable memory. Boot now requests Limine's RSDP response and records its base-revision-3 physical address only after confirming that its initial 20-byte span and complete page-rounded mapping extent are covered by ACPI-reclaimable or ACPI NVS memory-map regions and fit the reported physical width. The RSDP bytes are not read. Rustix can validate and enumerate addresses from an already-read RSDT/XSDT byte slice, but boot does not yet read or traverse those tables. It also does not initialize APIC hardware, configure interrupt routing, or enable interrupts.

## Required safe reader before hardware setup

`MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` bounds an ACPI byte span to 64 KiB, rounds it to 4 KiB mapping pages with checked arithmetic, and returns a validated physical mapping extent only if every byte of those pages is ACPI-reclaimable or ACPI NVS and within the known physical width. RSDT/XSDT parsing can enumerate table addresses without allocation, but the caller must validate each address and obtain a safe mapping before reading any target table. This is metadata validation, not a mapping or read operation. The future boot-time reader must use such validated extents and provide temporary read-only/NX mappings through an explicit checked mapping path. It must validate table lengths and checksums before copying bounded table data into owned kernel state. It must not use the HHDM or frame allocator as authorization to access arbitrary ACPI physical addresses. ACPI memory remains reserved until required table data has been copied and a separate reclamation policy is implemented.

MADT parsing currently supports the xAPIC processor records needed for the initial one-vCPU QEMU target. x2APIC processor records fail explicitly rather than being silently treated as xAPIC. APIC address ranges, duplicate identifiers, interrupt-source-override flags, and controller programming still require validation and policy before any interrupt-controller initialization.

# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, HHDM range arithmetic, and page-rounded ACPI span authorization. `MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` accepts at most 64 KiB of requested ACPI bytes and validates the entire 4 KiB-rounded physical extent against contiguous ACPI-reclaimable/NVS regions; this is metadata only, not a mapping or dereference grant. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.

`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf frames. It accepts only allocator-issued `Frame` tokens, requires NXE, supports four- and five-level paths, and holds one exclusive mutable borrow of its unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, rewrites inherited kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled so cached global translations cannot retain the previous alias permissions; the same invalidation is used if verification requires restoring the inherited root. Active candidates reject mapping, unmapping, and release; the type never writes CR3. Host tests cover clone ownership, huge-page splitting, cache-bit preservation, mutation guards, transactional map rollback, and retryable release failure. The QEMU adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked HHDM arithmetic.

The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot now rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when that CPUID leaf is available. For base revision 3 HHDM-mapped types, it also validates the page-rounded physical span, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. If the CPU does not report a physical width, the physical-bound check is skipped and no mapping caller may treat the bound as known. These checks are derived from metadata and Limine's protocol contract; they do not inspect page tables or prove that a non-null loader pointer is readable. HHDM dereferences are limited to the opt-in QEMU frame probe and candidate-table backend. Both first validate a complete allocator-owned `Usable` frame and its checked HHDM address, then rely narrowly on Limine's base-revision-3 guarantee; this is not a general physical-memory access service. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; executable kernel text must be explicit. MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. A page-table transition must preserve the kernel image, active stacks, boot data, descriptor tables, and any loader mappings still needed. Rustix does not reclaim bootloader memory or provide a general-purpose physical-memory service. It owns the page-table frames of the active cloned hierarchy but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The initial 256 KiB global heap is a bounded BSS arena and does not grow from physical frames. Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup and fatal exception diagnostics live in `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs`; they do not enable maskable IRQs.

## Active-root preservation and remaining limits

The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. The default boot path clones all reachable page-table pages into allocator-owned frames and preserves all leaf entries, then changes only the kernel-image HHDM alias permission bits while retaining cache attributes. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone

The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
4. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; the active cloned hierarchy owns its table frames, while the opt-in QEMU frame probe is the only general frame allocation test. Add active mapping services only after a TLB and mapping-lifetime policy exists.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active cloned hierarchy whose page-table frames it owns. The clone preserves Limine's mappings and applies R/NX or RW/NX permissions to kernel-image HHDM aliases. It is not a clean address-space rebuild, and general mapping/unmapping after activation is deliberately rejected without a TLB policy.
4. **Heap:** an initial global allocator uses a fixed 256 KiB BSS arena and at most 128 live allocations. It has deterministic exhaustion and exact-layout free semantics, does not grow from frames, and must not be called in interrupt context.
5. **Process address spaces:** isolate userspace; define copy-in/copy-out helpers and never treat user pointers as kernel references.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. The fixed BSS heap is bounded and non-growing. General mapping policy, broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.

//! Bounded, allocation-free ACPI structure validation and MADT parsing.
//!
//! These helpers consume byte slices supplied by a future checked table reader.
//! They do not map or dereference physical addresses and do not initialize APICs.

pub const MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE: usize = 64 * 1024;
const RSDP_V1_SIZE: usize = 20;
const RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE: usize = 36;
const SDT_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 36;
const MADT_FIXED_SIZE: usize = 44;
const MAX_MADT_ENTRIES: usize = 256;
pub const MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES: usize = 1024;
const MAX_LOCAL_APICS: usize = 16;
const MAX_IO_APICS: usize = 8;
const MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES: usize = 16;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiError {
    StructureTooShort,
    StructureTooLarge,
    InvalidRsdpSignature,
    InvalidRsdpChecksum,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpLength,
    InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum,
    UnsupportedRsdpRevision(u8),
    InvalidSdtLength,
    InvalidSdtChecksum,
    NotRootPointerTable,
    InvalidRootPointerTableLength,
    TooManyRootPointers,
    NullRootPointer,
    NotMadt,
    InvalidMadtLength,
    InvalidMadtEntryLength,
    TooManyMadtEntries,
    MadtCapacityExceeded,
    UnsupportedMadtEntryType(u8),
}

/// Validated root-system-description pointer fields copied out of the ACPI bytes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Rsdp {
    pub revision: u8,
    pub rsdt_address: u32,
    pub xsdt_address: Option<u64>,
}

impl Rsdp {
    /// Validate an RSDP byte slice and copy its table addresses.
    ///
    /// ACPI 1.0 (revision 0) structures use the 20-byte legacy checksum. ACPI
    /// 2.0+ structures must include and pass the extended checksum.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V1_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        if bytes[..8] != *b"RSD PTR " {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpSignature);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..RSDP_V1_SIZE]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpChecksum);
        }

        let revision = bytes[15];
        let rsdt_address = read_u32(bytes, 16);
        if revision == 0 {
            return Ok(Self {
                revision,
                rsdt_address,
                xsdt_address: None,
            });
        }
        if revision < 2 {
            return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedRsdpRevision(revision));
        }
        if bytes.len() < RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }

        let length = read_u32(bytes, 20) as usize;
        if !(RSDP_V2_MIN_SIZE..=MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE).contains(&length) || length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            revision,
            rsdt_address,
            xsdt_address: Some(read_u64(bytes, 24)),
        })
    }
}

/// A system-description table whose advertised length and checksum were checked.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Sdt<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    pub signature: [u8; 4],
    pub revision: u8,
}

impl<'a> Sdt<'a> {
    /// Validate an SDT header, bounded length, and checksum.
    ///
    /// Bytes following the advertised table length are ignored. The caller must
    /// still ensure that the complete advertised table is in the supplied slice.
    pub fn parse(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if bytes.len() < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooShort);
        }
        let length = read_u32(bytes, 4) as usize;
        if length < SDT_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if length > MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::StructureTooLarge);
        }
        if length > bytes.len() {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtLength);
        }
        if !checksum_is_valid(&bytes[..length]) {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            bytes: &bytes[..length],
            signature: [bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]],
            revision: bytes[8],
        })
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
        self.bytes.len()
    }

    pub fn root_pointer_table(self) -> Result<RootPointerTable<'a>, AcpiError> {
        RootPointerTable::parse(self)
    }
}

/// Bounded, zero-allocation view of an ACPI RSDT or XSDT address array.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RootPointerTable<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    entry_width: usize,
    entry_count: usize,
}

impl<'a> RootPointerTable<'a> {
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'a>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        let entry_width = match table.signature {
            [b'R', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 4,
            [b'X', b'S', b'D', b'T'] => 8,
            _ => return Err(AcpiError::NotRootPointerTable),
        };
        let payload_length = table.bytes.len() - SDT_HEADER_SIZE;
        if payload_length % entry_width != 0 {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength);
        }
        let entry_count = payload_length / entry_width;
        if entry_count > MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES {
            return Err(AcpiError::TooManyRootPointers);
        }
        let pointers = &table.bytes[SDT_HEADER_SIZE..];
        for index in 0..entry_count {
            let offset = index * entry_width;
            let address = if entry_width == 4 {
                read_u32(pointers, offset) as u64
            } else {
                read_u64(pointers, offset)
            };
            if address == 0 {
                return Err(AcpiError::NullRootPointer);
            }
        }
        Ok(Self {
            bytes: pointers,
            entry_width,
            entry_count,
        })
    }

    pub const fn is_xsdt(&self) -> bool {
        self.entry_width == 8
    }

    pub const fn entry_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.entry_count
    }

    pub fn address_at(&self, index: usize) -> Option<u64> {
        if index >= self.entry_count {
            return None;
        }
        let offset = index.checked_mul(self.entry_width)?;
        Some(if self.entry_width == 4 {
            read_u32(self.bytes, offset) as u64
        } else {
            read_u64(self.bytes, offset)
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LocalApic {
    pub processor_uid: u8,
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub flags: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IoApic {
    pub apic_id: u8,
    pub physical_address: u32,
    pub global_system_interrupt_base: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InterruptSourceOverride {
    pub bus: u8,
    pub source: u8,
    pub global_system_interrupt: u32,
    pub flags: u16,
}

/// Fixed-capacity, copied data from an xAPIC-compatible MADT.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Madt {
    pub local_apic_address: u64,
    pub flags: u32,
    local_apics: [Option<LocalApic>; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
    local_apic_count: usize,
    io_apics: [Option<IoApic>; MAX_IO_APICS],
    io_apic_count: usize,
    interrupt_overrides: [Option<InterruptSourceOverride>; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
    interrupt_override_count: usize,
}

impl Madt {
    /// Parse the known xAPIC MADT records into bounded owned arrays.
    ///
    /// Unknown record types are skipped after validating their common header.
    /// x2APIC processor records are rejected because this parser does not yet
    /// establish x2APIC mode or destination-ID policy.
    pub fn parse(table: Sdt<'_>) -> Result<Self, AcpiError> {
        if table.signature != *b"APIC" {
            return Err(AcpiError::NotMadt);
        }
        if table.bytes.len() < MADT_FIXED_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtLength);
        }

        let mut madt = Self {
            local_apic_address: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE) as u64,
            flags: read_u32(table.bytes, SDT_HEADER_SIZE + 4),
            local_apics: [None; MAX_LOCAL_APICS],
            local_apic_count: 0,
            io_apics: [None; MAX_IO_APICS],
            io_apic_count: 0,
            interrupt_overrides: [None; MAX_INTERRUPT_OVERRIDES],
            interrupt_override_count: 0,
        };

        let mut offset = MADT_FIXED_SIZE;
        let mut entry_count = 0;
        while offset < table.bytes.len() {
            if table.bytes.len() - offset < 2 {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            let entry_type = table.bytes[offset];
            let entry_length = table.bytes[offset + 1] as usize;
            if entry_length < 2 || entry_length > table.bytes.len() - offset {
                return Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength);
            }
            entry_count += 1;
            if entry_count > MAX_MADT_ENTRIES {
                return Err(AcpiError::TooManyMadtEntries);
            }

            let entry = &table.bytes[offset..offset + entry_length];
            match entry_type {
                0 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 8)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.local_apics,
                        &mut madt.local_apic_count,
                        LocalApic {
                            processor_uid: entry[2],
                            apic_id: entry[3],
                            flags: read_u32(entry, 4),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                1 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.io_apics,
                        &mut madt.io_apic_count,
                        IoApic {
                            apic_id: entry[2],
                            physical_address: read_u32(entry, 4),
                            global_system_interrupt_base: read_u32(entry, 8),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                2 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 10)?;
                    push(
                        &mut madt.interrupt_overrides,
                        &mut madt.interrupt_override_count,
                        InterruptSourceOverride {
                            bus: entry[2],
                            source: entry[3],
                            global_system_interrupt: read_u32(entry, 4),
                            flags: read_u16(entry, 8),
                        },
                    )?;
                }
                5 => {
                    require_entry_length(entry_length, 12)?;
                    madt.local_apic_address = read_u64(entry, 4);
                }
                9 => return Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedMadtEntryType(entry_type)),
                _ => {}
            }
            offset += entry_length;
        }

        Ok(madt)
    }

    pub fn local_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = LocalApic> + '_ {
        self.local_apics[..self.local_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn io_apics(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = IoApic> + '_ {
        self.io_apics[..self.io_apic_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }

    pub fn interrupt_overrides(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = InterruptSourceOverride> + '_ {
        self.interrupt_overrides[..self.interrupt_override_count]
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|entry| *entry)
    }
}

fn require_entry_length(actual: usize, expected: usize) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    if actual == expected {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength)
    }
}

fn push<T: Copy, const N: usize>(
    entries: &mut [Option<T>; N],
    count: &mut usize,
    value: T,
) -> Result<(), AcpiError> {
    let Some(slot) = entries.get_mut(*count) else {
        return Err(AcpiError::MadtCapacityExceeded);
    };
    *slot = Some(value);
    *count += 1;
    Ok(())
}

fn checksum_is_valid(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
    bytes.iter().fold(0u8, |sum, byte| sum.wrapping_add(*byte)) == 0
}

fn read_u16(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[offset], bytes[offset + 1]])
}

fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
    ])
}

fn read_u64(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes([
        bytes[offset],
        bytes[offset + 1],
        bytes[offset + 2],
        bytes[offset + 3],
        bytes[offset + 4],
        bytes[offset + 5],
        bytes[offset + 6],
        bytes[offset + 7],
    ])
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        AcpiError, Madt, Rsdp, Sdt, MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES, MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE, RSDP_V1_SIZE,
    };
    use core::assert_eq;
    extern crate std;

    fn set_checksum(bytes: &mut [u8], checksum_offset: usize, covered_length: usize) {
        bytes[checksum_offset] = 0;
        let sum = bytes[..covered_length]
            .iter()
            .fold(0u8, |sum, byte| sum.wrapping_add(*byte));
        bytes[checksum_offset] = 0u8.wrapping_sub(sum);
    }

    fn make_sdt(signature: [u8; 4], body: &[u8]) -> std::vec::Vec<u8> {
        let length = 36 + body.len();
        let mut bytes = std::vec![0; length];
        bytes[..4].copy_from_slice(&signature);
        bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&(length as u32).to_le_bytes());
        bytes[8] = 1;
        bytes[10..16].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[16..24].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX01");
        bytes[24..28].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[28..32].copy_from_slice(b"RUST");
        bytes[32..36].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[36..].copy_from_slice(body);
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 9, length);
        bytes
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_and_checksums_acpi_10_rsdp() {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 20];
        bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
        bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[15] = 0;
        bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);

        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Ok(Rsdp {
                revision: 0,
                rsdt_address: 0x1234_5000,
                xsdt_address: None,
            })
        );
        bytes[10] ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(Rsdp::parse(&bytes), Err(AcpiError::InvalidRsdpChecksum));
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_extended_rsdp_length_and_checksum() {
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 36];
        bytes[..8].copy_from_slice(b"RSD PTR ");
        bytes[9..15].copy_from_slice(b"RUSTIX");
        bytes[15] = 2;
        bytes[16..20].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[20..24].copy_from_slice(&36u32.to_le_bytes());
        bytes[24..32].copy_from_slice(&0x1234_5678_9000u64.to_le_bytes());
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 8, RSDP_V1_SIZE);
        set_checksum(&mut bytes, 32, 36);

        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Ok(Rsdp {
                revision: 2,
                rsdt_address: 0x1234_5000,
                xsdt_address: Some(0x1234_5678_9000),
            })
        );
        bytes[20..24].copy_from_slice(&(MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE as u32 + 1).to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            Rsdp::parse(&bytes),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidExtendedRsdpLength)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_sdt_length_and_checksum() {
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"TEST", &[1, 2, 3]);
        let table = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(table.signature, *b"TEST");
        assert_eq!(table.length(), 39);

        let mut corrupt = bytes;
        corrupt[36] ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(Sdt::parse(&corrupt), Err(AcpiError::InvalidSdtChecksum));
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_bounded_rsdt_and_xsdt_pointer_arrays() {
        let mut rsdt_body = std::vec::Vec::new();
        rsdt_body.extend_from_slice(&0x1234_5000u32.to_le_bytes());
        rsdt_body.extend_from_slice(&0x2345_6000u32.to_le_bytes());
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &rsdt_body);
        let pointers = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table().unwrap();
        assert!(!pointers.is_xsdt());
        assert_eq!(pointers.entry_count(), 2);
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(0), Some(0x1234_5000));
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(1), Some(0x2345_6000));
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(2), None);

        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"XSDT", &0x1_2345_6000u64.to_le_bytes());
        let pointers = Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table().unwrap();
        assert!(pointers.is_xsdt());
        assert_eq!(pointers.address_at(0), Some(0x1_2345_6000));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_malformed_rsdt_xsdt_pointers_and_capacity_overflow() {
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidRootPointerTableLength)
        );

        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"XSDT", &0u64.to_le_bytes());
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::NullRootPointer)
        );

        let mut pointers = std::vec![0x1000u32; MAX_ACPI_ROOT_ENTRIES + 1];
        let body = pointers
            .drain(..)
            .flat_map(u32::to_le_bytes)
            .collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>();
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"RSDT", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap().root_pointer_table(),
            Err(AcpiError::TooManyRootPointers)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_madt_devices_overrides_and_address_override() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body[0..4].copy_from_slice(&0xfee0_0000u32.to_le_bytes());
        body[4..8].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        body.extend_from_slice(&[0, 8, 1, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0]);
        body.extend_from_slice(&[1, 12, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        body[20..24].copy_from_slice(&0xfec0_0000u32.to_le_bytes());
        body[24..28].copy_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes());
        body.extend_from_slice(&[2, 10, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        body[32..36].copy_from_slice(&9u32.to_le_bytes());
        body.extend_from_slice(&[5, 12, 0, 0]);
        body.extend_from_slice(&0x1_0000_0000u64.to_le_bytes());

        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        let madt = Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(madt.local_apic_address, 0x1_0000_0000);
        assert_eq!(madt.flags, 1);
        assert_eq!(
            madt.local_apics().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::LocalApic {
                processor_uid: 1,
                apic_id: 2,
                flags: 1,
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            madt.io_apics().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::IoApic {
                apic_id: 3,
                physical_address: 0xfec0_0000,
                global_system_interrupt_base: 0,
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(
            madt.interrupt_overrides().collect::<std::vec::Vec<_>>(),
            [super::InterruptSourceOverride {
                bus: 0,
                source: 0,
                global_system_interrupt: 9,
                flags: 0,
            }]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_truncated_and_unsupported_madt_records() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body.extend_from_slice(&[1, 11, 0, 0]);
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::InvalidMadtEntryLength)
        );

        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        body.extend_from_slice(&[9, 2]);
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::UnsupportedMadtEntryType(9))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_fixed_madt_capacity_exhaustion() {
        let mut body = std::vec![0; 8];
        for apic_id in 0..17u8 {
            body.extend_from_slice(&[0, 8, apic_id, apic_id, 1, 0, 0, 0]);
        }
        let bytes = make_sdt(*b"APIC", &body);
        assert_eq!(
            Madt::parse(Sdt::parse(&bytes).unwrap()),
            Err(AcpiError::MadtCapacityExceeded)
        );
    }
}

# ACPI parsing foundation

## Current implementation

`src/acpi.rs` provides allocation-free helpers over caller-supplied byte slices:

- RSDP signature, legacy checksum, revision, bounded extended length, and extended checksum validation.
- System Description Table header, advertised-length, 64 KiB maximum-size, and checksum validation.
- Bounded, allocation-free RSDT/XSDT pointer-array views with entry-width, payload-length, null-entry, and count checks.
- Fixed-capacity copying of MADT local-APIC, I/O-APIC, interrupt-source-override, and local-APIC-address-override records.
- Structural rejection of malformed/truncated MADT records, unsupported x2APIC processor records, excessive entry counts, and fixed-array exhaustion.

These functions validate data already present in a byte slice. They neither follow physical addresses nor prove the slice came from ACPI-reclaimable memory. Boot now requests Limine's RSDP response and records its base-revision-3 physical address only after confirming that its initial 20-byte span and complete page-rounded mapping extent are covered by ACPI-reclaimable or ACPI NVS memory-map regions and fit the reported physical width. The RSDP bytes are not read. Rustix can validate and enumerate addresses from an already-read RSDT/XSDT byte slice, but boot does not yet read or traverse those tables. It also does not initialize APIC hardware, configure interrupt routing, or enable interrupts.

## Required safe reader before hardware setup

`MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` bounds an ACPI byte span to 64 KiB, rounds it to 4 KiB mapping pages with checked arithmetic, and returns a validated physical mapping extent only if every byte of those pages is ACPI-reclaimable or ACPI NVS and within the known physical width. RSDT/XSDT parsing can enumerate table addresses without allocation, but the caller must validate each address and obtain a safe mapping before reading any target table. This is metadata validation, not a mapping or read operation. The future boot-time reader must use such validated extents and provide temporary read-only/NX mappings through an explicit checked mapping path. It must validate table lengths and checksums before copying bounded table data into owned kernel state. It must not use the HHDM or frame allocator as authorization to access arbitrary ACPI physical addresses. ACPI memory remains reserved until required table data has been copied and a separate reclamation policy is implemented.

MADT parsing currently supports the xAPIC processor records needed for the initial one-vCPU QEMU target. x2APIC processor records fail explicitly rather than being silently treated as xAPIC. APIC address ranges, duplicate identifiers, interrupt-source-override flags, and controller programming still require validation and policy before any interrupt-controller initialization.

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [ACPI table parsing foundation](architecture/acpi.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. Hosted CI has not been observed. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the initial global heap uses a fixed 256 KiB BSS arena with 128 allocation records. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap is fixed-capacity and does not grow from frames; allocation is prohibited in interrupt context. ACPI groundwork now includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/MADT parsers and an optional Limine RSDP request; boot stores the base-revision-3 physical address only after validating its initial span and full page-rounded mapping extent against ACPI map regions and does not read the table bytes. There is no general IRQ subsystem, scheduler, process isolation, persistent filesystem, or Unix compatibility layer. Fatal CPU exceptions have basic GDT/TSS/IDT diagnostics but no recovery. `just fault-smoke` validates a controlled page fault (including CR2) and invalid opcode in QEMU; broader exception coverage and physical-hardware validation remain pending. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. These checks do not establish hosted-CI or physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

//! Host-testable ownership for x86 interrupt vectors reserved for device IRQs.
//!
//! Architectural exceptions occupy vectors 0–31. The upper range 0xf0–0xff is
//! kept unavailable for future local-APIC/spurious vectors; allocated vectors
//! therefore come only from 0x20–0xef. This allocator does not install IDT gates,
//! configure a controller, or enable interrupt delivery.

pub const FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR: u8 = 0x20;
pub const LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR: u8 = 0xef;
const VECTOR_COUNT: usize = 256;
const VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS: usize = VECTOR_COUNT / u64::BITS as usize;

/// A vector allocation token. Tokens are not `Copy` or `Clone` and must be
/// returned to the allocator instance that produced them.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InterruptVector(u8);

impl InterruptVector {
    pub const fn number(&self) -> u8 {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VectorReleaseError {
    ReservedVector,
    NotAllocated,
}

/// Failure to return a token preserves ownership by returning that token.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VectorReleaseFailure {
    pub error: VectorReleaseError,
    pub vector: InterruptVector,
}

/// Fixed-capacity allocator for vectors 0x20 through 0xef.
///
/// Only one allocator may manage a given CPU's vector namespace. The caller is
/// responsible for keeping it alive while any returned tokens are in use.
pub struct InterruptVectorAllocator {
    allocated: [u64; VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS],
    allocated_count: usize,
}

impl InterruptVectorAllocator {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        let mut allocated = [u64::MAX; VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS];
        let mut vector = FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR;
        while vector <= LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR {
            let word = vector as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
            let bit = vector as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
            allocated[word] &= !(1u64 << bit);
            vector += 1;
        }
        Self {
            allocated,
            allocated_count: 0,
        }
    }

    pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<InterruptVector> {
        for number in FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR..=LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR {
            let word = number as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
            let bit = number as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
            let mask = 1u64 << bit;
            if self.allocated[word] & mask == 0 {
                self.allocated[word] |= mask;
                self.allocated_count += 1;
                return Some(InterruptVector(number));
            }
        }
        None
    }

    pub fn release(
        &mut self,
        vector: InterruptVector,
    ) -> Result<(), VectorReleaseFailure> {
        if !(FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR..=LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR).contains(&vector.0) {
            return Err(VectorReleaseFailure {
                error: VectorReleaseError::ReservedVector,
                vector,
            });
        }
        let word = vector.0 as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
        let bit = vector.0 as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
        let mask = 1u64 << bit;
        if self.allocated[word] & mask == 0 {
            return Err(VectorReleaseFailure {
                error: VectorReleaseError::NotAllocated,
                vector,
            });
        }
        self.allocated[word] &= !mask;
        self.allocated_count -= 1;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub const fn allocated_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.allocated_count
    }
}

impl Default for InterruptVectorAllocator {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        InterruptVectorAllocator, VectorReleaseError, FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR, LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR,
    };
    use core::assert_eq;

    #[test]
    fn allocates_only_from_the_device_vector_range() {
        let mut allocator = InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
        let first = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(first.number(), FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR);

        for expected in (FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR + 1)..=LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR {
            assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().number(), expected);
        }
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocated_count(), 208);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn released_vectors_are_reused_without_leaking_tokens_on_failure() {
        let mut allocator = InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
        let token = allocator.allocate().unwrap();
        let number = token.number();
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocated_count(), 1);

        allocator.release(token).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocated_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate().unwrap().number(), number);
    }

    #[test]
    fn allocation_exhaustion_is_bounded_and_deterministic() {
        let mut allocator = InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
        let mut count = 0;
        while allocator.allocate().is_some() {
            count += 1;
        }
        assert_eq!(count, 208);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocated_count(), count);
        assert_eq!(allocator.allocate(), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn failed_release_returns_the_unmodified_vector_token() {
        let mut first = InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
        let mut second = InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
        let token = first.allocate().unwrap();
        let failure = second.release(token).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(failure.error, VectorReleaseError::NotAllocated);
        assert_eq!(failure.vector.number(), FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR);
        assert_eq!(second.allocated_count(), 0);
        assert_eq!(first.allocated_count(), 1);
    }
}
