#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(feature = "inject-page-fault", feature = "inject-invalid-opcode"))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
        &reader,
        inherited_root,
        config,
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Some(rsdp_physical_address) = boot_info.rsdp_physical_address {
        match load_acpi_madt(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            rsdp_physical_address,
            new_cr3,
            inherited_cr3,
        ) {
            Ok(madt) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC={:#x}, {} local APICs, {} I/O APICs, {} overrides",
                    madt.local_apic_address,
                    madt.local_apics().count(),
                    madt.io_apics().count(),
                    madt.interrupt_overrides().count()
                );
                boot_info.acpi_madt = Some(madt);
            }
            Err(error) => kprintln!("ACPI MADT unavailable: {:?}", error),
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts are disabled from bootstrap initialization onward.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );
    probe_kernel_heap();

    // Keep the candidate and its frame tokens alive for as long as this root is
    // active. The shell runs forever and does not return to this stack frame.
    // SAFETY: The bootstrap is single-core, interrupts remain disabled, and the
    // shell is the only filesystem owner.
    let filesystem = unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RAM_FILESYSTEM) };
    match filesystem.seed_defaults() {
        Ok(home) => shell::run(filesystem, home, boot_info),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("RAM filesystem initialization failed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever()
        }
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiBootReadError {
    PhysicalWidthUnknown,
    PatUnavailable,
    InvalidPat(rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayoutError),
    InvalidMtrr(rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrError),
    MtrrUnavailable,
    NoVirtualWindow,
    PageTableWalk,
    Read(rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiReadError<AcpiMappingError>),
}

fn load_acpi_madt<'candidate, 'memory, 'map>(
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    cpu_info: &arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    rsdp_physical_address: u64,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
) -> Result<rustix_kernel::acpi::Madt, AcpiBootReadError> {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{MtrrState, PageWalkOutcome, PatLayout};

    let physical_address_bits = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or(AcpiBootReadError::PhysicalWidthUnknown)?;
    let pat_value = cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .ok_or(AcpiBootReadError::PatUnavailable)?;
    let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).map_err(AcpiBootReadError::InvalidPat)?;
    let cache_layout = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_address_bits)
            .map_err(AcpiBootReadError::InvalidMtrr)?,
        _ => return Err(AcpiBootReadError::MtrrUnavailable),
    };

    const WINDOW_BASE: u64 = 0xffff_c000_0000_0000;
    const WINDOW_PAGES: u64 = 4096;
    let mut virtual_address = WINDOW_BASE;
    let mut window_found = false;
    for _ in 0..WINDOW_PAGES {
        match candidate.walk(virtual_address) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. }) => {
                window_found = true;
                break;
            }
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(_)) => {}
            Err(_) => return Err(AcpiBootReadError::PageTableWalk),
        }
        virtual_address = virtual_address
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(AcpiBootReadError::NoVirtualWindow)?;
    }
    if !window_found {
        return Err(AcpiBootReadError::NoVirtualWindow);
    }

    let mut reader = CandidateAcpiReader {
        candidate,
        allocator,
        memory_map,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        cache_layout,
        pat,
        normal_caching: cpu_info.normal_caching,
        candidate_cr3,
        previous_cr3,
        virtual_address,
    };
    let mut scratch = [0u8; rustix_kernel::acpi::MAX_ACPI_STRUCTURE_SIZE];
    rustix_kernel::acpi::read_madt(&mut reader, rsdp_physical_address, &mut scratch)
        .map_err(AcpiBootReadError::Read)
}

fn harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    segments: rustix_kernel::memory::KernelImageSegments,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    inherited_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        walk_virtual_address, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let image_segments = [
        ("kernel text", segments.text, false),
        ("kernel rodata", segments.rodata, false),
        ("kernel data", segments.data, true),
    ];
    for (label, segment, writable) in image_segments {
        let length = segment.physical_end - segment.physical_start;
        let mut offset = 0;
        while offset < length {
            let Some(physical_address) = segment.physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
                kprintln!(
                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                return false;
            };
            let alias = match memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
                hhdm_offset,
                physical_address,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                physical_address_bits,
                virtual_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(alias) => alias,
                Err(error) => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} address: {:?}",
                        label,
                        error
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            };
            let source = match walk_virtual_address(reader, inherited_root, alias, config) {
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
                result => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} inherited walk: {:?}",
                        label,
                        result
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            };
            let permissions = PagePermissions {
                writable,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: false,
            };
            if let Err(error) = candidate.set_inherited_page_permissions(
                allocator,
                alias,
                physical_address,
                permissions,
            ) {
                kprintln!(
                    "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} protection: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                return false;
            }
            match candidate.walk(alias) {
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_address
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
                        && translation.pat_index == source.pat_index => {}
                result => {
                    kprintln!(
                        "kernel HHDM alias check failed: {} candidate walk: {:?}",
                        label,
                        result
                    );
                    return false;
                }
            }
            offset += PAGE_SIZE;
        }
    }
    true
}

fn probe_kernel_heap() {
    use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};

    let full_layout = match Layout::from_size_align(rustix_kernel::heap::KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, 1) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "kernel heap probe failed to construct full-arena layout: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap static is initialized before use and maskable interrupts
    // remain disabled; this probe requests a valid nonzero layout.
    let full_arena = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(full_layout) };
    if full_arena.is_null() {
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: full-arena allocation was rejected");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let small_layout = Layout::new::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: The heap lock serializes this valid nonzero allocation request.
    let exhausted = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(small_layout) };
    if !exhausted.is_null() {
        // SAFETY: Both pointers are live allocations with their original layouts.
        unsafe {
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(exhausted, small_layout);
            KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout);
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: exhaustion was not deterministic");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: `full_arena` is the complete live allocation created above.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(full_arena, full_layout) };

    let layout = match Layout::from_size_align(257, 64) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "kernel heap probe failed to construct aligned layout: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The heap is available after releasing the full-arena allocation.
    let allocation = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if allocation.is_null() || allocation as usize % layout.align() != 0 {
        if !allocation.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: This is the live allocation returned for `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: aligned allocation was rejected or misaligned");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocator returned `layout.size()` writable bytes.
    unsafe { core::ptr::write_bytes(allocation, 0xa5, layout.size()) };
    for index in 0..layout.size() {
        // SAFETY: `index` remains inside the live allocation.
        if unsafe { allocation.add(index).read_volatile() } != 0xa5 {
            // SAFETY: The allocation is still live with its original layout.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
            kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: allocation data did not round-trip");
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The allocation is live and the original layout is supplied.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(allocation, layout) };
    // SAFETY: The previous allocation was returned; first-fit should reuse it.
    let reused = unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.alloc(layout) };
    if reused != allocation {
        if !reused.is_null() {
            // SAFETY: `reused` is a live allocation with `layout`.
            unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
        }
        kprintln!("kernel heap probe failed: freed space was not reused");
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The reused allocation is live and has the same layout.
    unsafe { KERNEL_HEAP.dealloc(reused, layout) };
    kprintln!("kernel heap probe passed: alignment, reuse, deterministic exhaustion");
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    let mut verified = true;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        // The CPU may update Accessed/Dirty in the active hierarchy after the
        // clone; they are hardware tracking state, not translation policy.
        let hardware_tracking_bits = (1 << 5) | (1 << 6);
        if source_translation.physical_address != candidate_translation.physical_address
            || source_translation.leaf_physical_base != candidate_translation.leaf_physical_base
            || source_translation.page_size != candidate_translation.page_size
            || source_translation.permissions != candidate_translation.permissions
            || source_translation.pat_index != candidate_translation.pat_index
            || source_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
                != candidate_translation.raw_leaf_entry & !hardware_tracking_bits
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

//! Allocation-free validation for virtual addresses and physical memory maps.

/// Limine's memory-map type for ordinary usable RAM.
pub const MEMORY_MAP_USABLE: u64 = 0;
/// Maximum number of memory regions retained in the boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS: usize = 256;
/// Minimum x86_64 initial stack size guaranteed by the Limine protocol.
pub const LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

/// Check whether an address is canonical for a sign-extended virtual width.
///
/// Widths outside `1..=64` are rejected. A 64-bit width accepts every address.
pub const fn is_canonical_virtual_address(address: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    if address_bits == 64 {
        return true;
    }

    let sign_bit = (address >> (address_bits - 1)) & 1;
    let upper_bits = address >> address_bits;
    let expected_upper_bits = if sign_bit == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        u64::MAX >> address_bits
    };
    upper_bits == expected_upper_bits
}

/// Check that a non-empty half-open physical range fits an address width.
pub const fn physical_range_fits_address_width(start: u64, end: u64, address_bits: u8) -> bool {
    if start >= end || address_bits == 0 || address_bits > 64 {
        return false;
    }
    address_bits == 64 || end <= (1u64 << address_bits)
}

/// Return the physical end of the linker-defined kernel image span, if valid.
///
/// Limine reports the load bases while the linker supplies the virtual span.
/// This validates that both sources agree on the virtual base and that the
/// relocated half-open physical range fits the known address widths.
pub const fn kernel_image_physical_end(
    physical_base: u64,
    reported_virtual_base: u64,
    linked_virtual_start: u64,
    linked_virtual_end: u64,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> Option<u64> {
    if linked_virtual_start != reported_virtual_base
        || linked_virtual_start >= linked_virtual_end
        || physical_base & 0xfff != 0
        || linked_virtual_start & 0xfff != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let virtual_last = linked_virtual_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(linked_virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    if linked_virtual_start & sign_bit != virtual_last & sign_bit {
        return None;
    }

    let image_size = linked_virtual_end - linked_virtual_start;
    let Some(physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(image_size) else {
        return None;
    };
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_base, physical_end, bits) {
            return None;
        }
    }
    Some(physical_end)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KernelImageVirtualSegments {
    pub text: (u64, u64),
    pub rodata: (u64, u64),
    pub data: (u64, u64),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KernelImageSegment {
    pub virtual_start: u64,
    pub virtual_end: u64,
    pub physical_start: u64,
    pub physical_end: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KernelImageSegments {
    pub text: KernelImageSegment,
    pub rodata: KernelImageSegment,
    pub data: KernelImageSegment,
}

/// Validate page-aligned PT_LOAD mapping spans and translate them to physical ranges.
///
/// The three spans must be contiguous, ordered text/rodata/data ranges that cover
/// the linker-defined image after rounding its final byte to a 4 KiB boundary.
/// This validates linker metadata; it does not prove that inherited page tables
/// map these ranges or that their backing frames are owned by Rustix.
pub const fn kernel_image_segments(
    physical_base: u64,
    reported_virtual_base: u64,
    image_virtual_start: u64,
    image_virtual_end: u64,
    virtual_segments: KernelImageVirtualSegments,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> Option<KernelImageSegments> {
    let Some(_) = kernel_image_physical_end(
        physical_base,
        reported_virtual_base,
        image_virtual_start,
        image_virtual_end,
        physical_bits,
        virtual_bits,
    ) else {
        return None;
    };

    let (text_start, text_end) = virtual_segments.text;
    let (rodata_start, rodata_end) = virtual_segments.rodata;
    let (data_start, data_end) = virtual_segments.data;
    if text_start != image_virtual_start
        || text_start >= text_end
        || text_end != rodata_start
        || rodata_start >= rodata_end
        || rodata_end != data_start
        || data_start >= image_virtual_end
        || image_virtual_end > data_end
    {
        return None;
    }

    let Some(rounded_image_end) = image_virtual_end.checked_add(0xfff) else {
        return None;
    };
    let rounded_image_end = rounded_image_end & !0xfff;
    if data_end != rounded_image_end
        || text_start & 0xfff != 0
        || text_end & 0xfff != 0
        || rodata_start & 0xfff != 0
        || rodata_end & 0xfff != 0
        || data_start & 0xfff != 0
        || data_end & 0xfff != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let mapped_last_virtual = data_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(image_virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(mapped_last_virtual, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    if virtual_bits < 64
        && ((image_virtual_start ^ mapped_last_virtual) & (1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1))) != 0
    {
        return None;
    }

    let Some(mapped_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(data_end - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_base, mapped_physical_end, bits) {
            return None;
        }
    }

    let Some(text_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(text_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(text_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(text_end - image_virtual_start) else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(rodata_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(rodata_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(rodata_physical_end) = physical_base.checked_add(rodata_end - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };
    let Some(data_physical_start) = physical_base.checked_add(data_start - image_virtual_start)
    else {
        return None;
    };

    Some(KernelImageSegments {
        text: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: text_start,
            virtual_end: text_end,
            physical_start: text_physical_start,
            physical_end: text_physical_end,
        },
        rodata: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: rodata_start,
            virtual_end: rodata_end,
            physical_start: rodata_physical_start,
            physical_end: rodata_physical_end,
        },
        data: KernelImageSegment {
            virtual_start: data_start,
            virtual_end: data_end,
            physical_start: data_physical_start,
            physical_end: mapped_physical_end,
        },
    })
}

/// Derive the requested initial x86_64 stack span below Limine's entry RSP.
///
/// The SysV entry stack has an 8-byte return-address slot, so `entry_rsp + 8`
/// is the exclusive top. The requested span must be at least the protocol's
/// 64 KiB minimum; callers should pass the size actually requested from Limine.
pub const fn limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(
    entry_rsp: u64,
    virtual_bits: u8,
    stack_size: u64,
) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
    if entry_rsp & 0xf != 8 {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_end) = entry_rsp.checked_add(8) else {
        return None;
    };
    if stack_size < LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_start) = stack_end.checked_sub(stack_size) else {
        return None;
    };
    let stack_last = stack_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    if stack_start & sign_bit != stack_last & sign_bit {
        return None;
    }
    Some((stack_start, stack_end))
}

/// Validate the page-rounded HHDM span for one Limine base-revision-3 region.
///
/// `physical_bits` is `None` only when CPUID does not report the width. This
/// checks arithmetic and canonicality, not whether the inherited page tables
/// actually contain the mapping.
pub const fn limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
    offset: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_bits: u8,
) -> bool {
    const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
    const PAGE_MASK: u64 = !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);

    if physical_start >= physical_end
        || offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || (virtual_bits != 48 && virtual_bits != 57)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(offset, virtual_bits)
    {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(physical_start, physical_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let mapped_start = physical_start & PAGE_MASK;
    let Some(rounded_end) = physical_end.checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    let mapped_end = rounded_end & PAGE_MASK;
    if mapped_start >= mapped_end {
        return false;
    }
    if let Some(bits) = physical_bits {
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapped_start, mapped_end, bits) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    let Some(virtual_start) = offset.checked_add(mapped_start) else {
        return false;
    };
    let Some(virtual_last) = offset.checked_add(mapped_end - 1) else {
        return false;
    };
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return false;
    }

    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    virtual_start & sign_bit == virtual_last & sign_bit
}

/// Classification of a physical memory region from the Limine memory map.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RegionKind {
    Usable,
    Reserved,
    AcpiReclaimable,
    AcpiNvs,
    BadMemory,
    BootloaderReclaimable,
    ExecutableAndModules,
    Framebuffer,
    Unknown(u64),
}

impl RegionKind {
    /// Whether Limine base revision 3 includes this type in the HHDM.
    pub const fn is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm(self) -> bool {
        matches!(
            self,
            Self::Usable
                | Self::BootloaderReclaimable
                | Self::ExecutableAndModules
                | Self::Framebuffer
        )
    }

    const fn from_limine(kind: u64) -> Self {
        match kind {
            0 => Self::Usable,
            1 => Self::Reserved,
            2 => Self::AcpiReclaimable,
            3 => Self::AcpiNvs,
            4 => Self::BadMemory,
            5 => Self::BootloaderReclaimable,
            6 => Self::ExecutableAndModules,
            7 => Self::Framebuffer,
            unknown => Self::Unknown(unknown),
        }
    }
}

/// Unvalidated region fields copied from a boot protocol response.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RawMemoryRegion {
    pub base: u64,
    pub length: u64,
    pub kind: u64,
}

/// Validated half-open physical address range `[start, end)`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PhysicalRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: RegionKind,
}

impl PhysicalRegion {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        start: 0,
        end: 0,
        kind: RegionKind::Unknown(0),
    };

    pub const fn start(&self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(&self) -> RegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

/// Errors produced when a memory map is malformed or exceeds kernel capacity.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MemoryMapError {
    EmptyMap,
    TooManyRegions,
    EmptyRegion { index: usize },
    AddressOverflow { index: usize },
    OverlappingRegions { first: usize, second: usize },
    UsableTotalOverflow,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HhdmAddressError {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NotUsable,
    NotLimineMapped,
    InvalidHhdmRange,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AcpiSpanError {
    EmptyRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    SpanTooLarge,
    PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds,
    NotFullyAcpiBacked,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum AcpiSpanAuthorization {
    AcpiTableMemory,
    LegacyRsdpReserved,
}

/// A physical ACPI-related byte span whose complete 4 KiB mapping extent has
/// explicit memory-map authorization and fits the known physical-address width.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedAcpiSpan {
    byte_start: u64,
    byte_end: u64,
    mapping_start: u64,
    mapping_end: u64,
    authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization,
}

impl ValidatedAcpiSpan {
    pub const fn byte_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.byte_start
    }

    pub const fn byte_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.byte_end
    }

    pub const fn mapping_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_start
    }

    pub const fn mapping_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.mapping_end
    }

    /// Whether one aligned 4 KiB physical page is fully covered by this span's
    /// validated page-rounded mapping extent.
    pub fn contains_mapping_page(self, physical_page: u64) -> bool {
        if physical_page & 0xfff != 0 {
            return false;
        }
        let Some(page_end) = physical_page.checked_add(4096) else {
            return false;
        };
        let authorization_contains_page = match self.authorization {
            AcpiSpanAuthorization::AcpiTableMemory => true,
            AcpiSpanAuthorization::LegacyRsdpReserved => {
                physical_page >= 0x80_000 && page_end <= 0x10_0000
            }
        };
        authorization_contains_page
            && physical_page >= self.mapping_start
            && page_end <= self.mapping_end
    }
}

/// Validated, allocation-free snapshot of the physical memory map.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MemoryMap {
    regions: [PhysicalRegion; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
    region_count: usize,
    usable_bytes: u64,
}

impl MemoryMap {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        regions: [PhysicalRegion::EMPTY; MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS],
        region_count: 0,
        usable_bytes: 0,
    };

    pub fn from_raw(regions: &[RawMemoryRegion]) -> Result<Self, MemoryMapError> {
        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for region in regions {
            builder.push(region.base, region.length, region.kind)?;
        }
        builder.finish()
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> &[PhysicalRegion] {
        &self.regions[..self.region_count]
    }

    pub fn range_is_within_region_kind(&self, start: u64, end: u64, kind: RegionKind) -> bool {
        start < end
            && self
                .regions()
                .iter()
                .any(|region| region.start <= start && end <= region.end && region.kind == kind)
    }

    /// Check that a non-empty physical span is covered only by ACPI reclaimable
    /// or ACPI NVS regions, optionally enforcing the reported physical width.
    /// Adjacent ACPI regions may jointly cover the span; gaps and other region
    /// kinds are rejected. This checks metadata only and does not authorize a
    /// dereference or imply that the span is mapped.
    pub fn validate_acpi_span(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedAcpiSpan, AcpiSpanError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
        const MAX_SPAN_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if length > MAX_SPAN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if physical_address_bits
            .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        let mapping_start = start & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mapping_end = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if mapping_end <= mapping_start {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow);
        }
        if physical_address_bits.is_some_and(|bits| {
            !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapping_start, mapping_end, bits)
        }) {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        if !self.range_is_within_acpi_regions(mapping_start, mapping_end, physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked);
        }

        Ok(ValidatedAcpiSpan {
            byte_start: start,
            byte_end: end,
            mapping_start,
            mapping_end,
            authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization::AcpiTableMemory,
        })
    }

    /// Validate an RSDP span in ACPI memory or in the bounded legacy x86
    /// firmware window `[0x80000, 0x100000)`. The legacy exception is only for
    /// the RSDP itself; table addresses must use `validate_acpi_span`.
    pub fn validate_rsdp_span(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedAcpiSpan, AcpiSpanError> {
        if let Ok(span) = self.validate_acpi_span(start, length, physical_address_bits) {
            return Ok(span);
        }
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;
        const LEGACY_RSDP_START: u64 = 0x80_000;
        const LEGACY_RSDP_END: u64 = 0x10_0000;
        const MAX_SPAN_SIZE: u64 = 64 * 1024;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if length > MAX_SPAN_SIZE {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if physical_address_bits
            .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds);
        }
        let mapping_start = start & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        let mapping_end = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE - 1)
            .ok_or(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if mapping_end <= mapping_start {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow);
        }
        if mapping_start < LEGACY_RSDP_START
            || mapping_end > LEGACY_RSDP_END
            || physical_address_bits.is_some_and(|bits| {
                !physical_range_fits_address_width(mapping_start, mapping_end, bits)
            })
            || !self.range_is_covered_by_kind(mapping_start, mapping_end, RegionKind::Reserved)
        {
            return Err(AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked);
        }

        Ok(ValidatedAcpiSpan {
            byte_start: start,
            byte_end: end,
            mapping_start,
            mapping_end,
            authorization: AcpiSpanAuthorization::LegacyRsdpReserved,
        })
    }

    fn range_is_covered_by_kind(&self, start: u64, end: u64, kind: RegionKind) -> bool {
        if start >= end {
            return false;
        }
        let mut covered_until = start;
        for region in self.regions() {
            if region.end <= covered_until {
                continue;
            }
            if region.start > covered_until || region.kind != kind {
                return false;
            }
            covered_until = region.end.min(end);
            if covered_until == end {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    pub fn range_is_within_acpi_regions(
        &self,
        start: u64,
        end: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    ) -> bool {
        if start >= end
            || physical_address_bits
                .is_some_and(|bits| !physical_range_fits_address_width(start, end, bits))
        {
            return false;
        }

        let mut covered_until = start;
        for region in self.regions() {
            if region.end <= covered_until {
                continue;
            }
            if region.start > covered_until
                || !matches!(
                    region.kind,
                    RegionKind::AcpiReclaimable | RegionKind::AcpiNvs
                )
            {
                return false;
            }
            covered_until = region.end.min(end);
            if covered_until == end {
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    /// Calculate the Limine base-revision-3 HHDM address of a page-aligned
    /// extent wholly contained in one region that Limine maps into the HHDM.
    ///
    /// This validates metadata and relies on the Limine handoff contract for the
    /// actual mapping; it does not inspect inherited page tables or make the
    /// returned integer safe to dereference by itself.
    pub fn limine_hhdm_address(
        &self,
        hhdm_offset: u64,
        physical_start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<u64, HhdmAddressError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

        let physical_address_bits =
            physical_address_bits.ok_or(HhdmAddressError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let physical_end = physical_start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.regions().iter().any(|region| {
            region.start <= physical_start
                && physical_end <= region.end
                && region.kind.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm()
        }) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        if !limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            physical_end,
            Some(physical_address_bits),
            virtual_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        hhdm_offset
            .checked_add(physical_start)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange)
    }

    /// Calculate the HHDM address of a page-aligned extent wholly contained in
    /// validated `Usable` memory.
    pub fn usable_hhdm_address(
        &self,
        hhdm_offset: u64,
        physical_start: u64,
        length: u64,
        physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<u64, HhdmAddressError> {
        const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

        if length == 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let physical_end = physical_start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.range_is_within_region_kind(physical_start, physical_end, RegionKind::Usable) {
            return Err(HhdmAddressError::NotUsable);
        }
        self.limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            length,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    pub const fn usable_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        self.usable_bytes
    }
}

/// Incremental validator used to copy loader entries without an intermediate heap.
pub struct MemoryMapBuilder {
    map: MemoryMap,
}

impl MemoryMapBuilder {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: MemoryMap::EMPTY,
        }
    }

    pub fn push(&mut self, base: u64, length: u64, raw_kind: u64) -> Result<(), MemoryMapError> {
        let index = self.map.region_count;
        if index == MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index });
        }
        let end = base
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index })?;
        let kind = RegionKind::from_limine(raw_kind);

        for (other_index, other) in self.map.regions().iter().enumerate() {
            if base < other.end && other.start < end {
                return Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                    first: other_index,
                    second: index,
                });
            }
        }

        let usable_bytes = if kind == RegionKind::Usable {
            self.map
                .usable_bytes
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(MemoryMapError::UsableTotalOverflow)?
        } else {
            self.map.usable_bytes
        };

        self.map.regions[index] = PhysicalRegion {
            start: base,
            end,
            kind,
        };
        self.map.region_count += 1;
        self.map.usable_bytes = usable_bytes;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<MemoryMap, MemoryMapError> {
        if self.map.region_count == 0 {
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap)
        } else {
            Ok(self.map)
        }
    }
}

impl Default for MemoryMapBuilder {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Add an already-validated usable region length to a running total.
///
/// Non-usable regions leave the total unchanged. `None` signals arithmetic
/// overflow so callers can report malformed or unrepresentable maps.
pub const fn add_usable_bytes(total: u64, region_kind: u64, region_length: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if region_kind == MEMORY_MAP_USABLE {
        total.checked_add(region_length)
    } else {
        Some(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use core::assert_eq;

    use super::{
        add_usable_bytes, is_canonical_virtual_address, kernel_image_physical_end,
        kernel_image_segments, limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid, limine_x86_64_stack_bounds,
        physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, KernelImageSegment,
        KernelImageSegments, KernelImageVirtualSegments, MemoryMap, MemoryMapBuilder,
