    #[test]
    fn canonical_virtual_addresses_follow_the_selected_width() {
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0000_7fff_ffff_ffff, 48));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0000_8000_0000_0000, 48));
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0xffff_8000_0000_0000, 48));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0xffff_7fff_ffff_ffff, 48));

        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0x00ff_ffff_ffff_ffff, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0x0100_0000_0000_0000, 57));
        assert!(is_canonical_virtual_address(0xff00_0000_0000_0000, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0xfeff_ffff_ffff_ffff, 57));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0, 0));
        assert!(!is_canonical_virtual_address(0, 65));
    }

    #[test]
    fn physical_ranges_fit_the_reported_address_width() {
        assert!(physical_range_fits_address_width(0x1000, 1 << 40, 40));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(
            0x1000,
            (1 << 40) + 1,
            40
        ));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(1, 1, 40));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(0, 1, 0));
        assert!(!physical_range_fits_address_width(0, 1, 65));
        assert!(physical_range_fits_address_width(
            u64::MAX - 1,
            u64::MAX,
            64
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn relocates_and_validates_the_linker_defined_kernel_image_span() {
        let virtual_base = 0xffff_ffff_8000_0000;
        let virtual_end = 0xffff_ffff_8002_5050;
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                0x0fee_3000,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_end,
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            Some(0x0ff0_8050)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                0x1000,
                virtual_base + 0x1000,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_end,
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(0x1000, virtual_base, virtual_base, virtual_base, None, 48),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                0xffff_ffff_ffff_f000,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base + 0x2000,
                None,
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                0x1001,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base + 0x1000,
                None,
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                (1 << 40) - 0x1000,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base,
                virtual_base + 0x2000,
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_physical_end(
                0x1000,
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
                0xffff_8000_0000_1000,
                None,
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_and_relocates_page_aligned_kernel_load_segments() {
        let virtual_start = 0xffff_ffff_8000_0000;
        let virtual_end = 0xffff_ffff_8000_5050;
        let segments = kernel_image_segments(
            0x20_0000,
            virtual_start,
            virtual_start,
            virtual_end,
            KernelImageVirtualSegments {
                text: (virtual_start, virtual_start + 0x2000),
                rodata: (virtual_start + 0x2000, virtual_start + 0x4000),
                data: (virtual_start + 0x4000, virtual_start + 0x6000),
            },
            Some(40),
            48,
        )
        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            segments,
            KernelImageSegments {
                text: KernelImageSegment {
                    virtual_start,
                    virtual_end: virtual_start + 0x2000,
                    physical_start: 0x20_0000,
                    physical_end: 0x20_2000,
                },
                rodata: KernelImageSegment {
                    virtual_start: virtual_start + 0x2000,
                    virtual_end: virtual_start + 0x4000,
                    physical_start: 0x20_2000,
                    physical_end: 0x20_4000,
                },
                data: KernelImageSegment {
                    virtual_start: virtual_start + 0x4000,
                    virtual_end: virtual_start + 0x6000,
                    physical_start: 0x20_4000,
                    physical_end: 0x20_6000,
                },
            }
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_page_aligned_kernel_load_segments() {
        let virtual_start = 0xffff_ffff_8000_0000;
        let virtual_end = virtual_start + 0x5050;
        let valid = KernelImageVirtualSegments {
            text: (virtual_start, virtual_start + 0x2000),
            rodata: (virtual_start + 0x2000, virtual_start + 0x4000),
            data: (virtual_start + 0x4000, virtual_start + 0x6000),
        };
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_segments(
                0x20_0000,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_end,
                KernelImageVirtualSegments {
                    rodata: (virtual_start + 0x3000, virtual_start + 0x4000),
                    ..valid
                },
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_segments(
                0x20_0000,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_end,
                KernelImageVirtualSegments {
                    text: (virtual_start, virtual_start + 0x2001),
                    rodata: (virtual_start + 0x2001, virtual_start + 0x4000),
                    ..valid
                },
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kernel_image_segments(
                0x20_0000,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_start,
                virtual_end,
                KernelImageVirtualSegments {
                    data: (virtual_start + 0x4000, virtual_start + 0x5000),
                    ..valid
                },
                Some(40),
                48,
            ),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn derives_protocol_guaranteed_initial_stack_bounds() {
        let entry_rsp = 0xffff_8000_0001_fff8;
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            Some((0xffff_8000_0001_0000, 0xffff_8000_0002_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x0000_7fff_ffff_fff8, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE,),
            Some((0x0000_7fff_ffff_0000, 0x0000_8000_0000_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, 57, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            Some((0xffff_8000_0001_0000, 0xffff_8000_0002_0000))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE - 1),
            None
        );
        let large_stack_top = 0xffff_8000_0006_0000;
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(large_stack_top - 8, 48, 256 * 1024),
            Some((0xffff_8000_0002_0000, large_stack_top))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(entry_rsp & !0xf, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(u64::MAX - 7, 64, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x0000_8000_0000_0008, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(
            limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(0x10008, 48, LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE),
            Some((0x10, 0x10010))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_page_rounded_limine_hhdm_ranges_without_accessing_them() {
        let offset = 0xffff_8000_0000_0000;
        assert!(limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset,
            0x1234,
            0x2345,
            Some(40),
            48
        ));
        assert!(limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset, 0x1234, 0x2345, None, 48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset,
            0x1234,
            (1 << 40) + 1,
            Some(40),
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            u64::MAX - 0x0fff,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            None,
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
            0x1000,
            0x2000,
            None,
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            0,
            0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000,
            0x0000_8000_0000_1000,
            Some(64),
            48
        ));
        assert!(!limine_v3_hhdm_range_is_valid(
            offset, 0x1000, 0x2000, None, 46
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn calculates_usable_hhdm_addresses_only_for_validated_owned_ranges() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: 0x3000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_3000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let offset = 0xffff_8000_0000_0000;

        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_1000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Ok(offset + 0x10_1000)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_3000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::NotUsable)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0001, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0000, 0, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::EmptyRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, 0x10_0000, 0x1000, None, 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(offset, u64::MAX & !0xfff, 0x1000, Some(64), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.usable_hhdm_address(0x0000_8000_0000_0000, 0x10_0000, 0x1000, Some(40), 48),
            Err(HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn classifies_limine_v3_hhdm_region_types() {
        assert!(RegionKind::Usable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::ExecutableAndModules.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(RegionKind::Framebuffer.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Reserved.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiReclaimable.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::AcpiNvs.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::BadMemory.is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
        assert!(!RegionKind::Unknown(99).is_mapped_by_limine_v3_hhdm());
    }

    #[test]
    fn counts_only_usable_regions() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 2048), Some(6144));
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(4096, 1, 2048), Some(4096));
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_total_overflow() {
        assert_eq!(add_usable_bytes(u64::MAX - 4, MEMORY_MAP_USABLE, 8), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_ranges_and_preserves_all_region_kinds() {
        let raw = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x2000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x4000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 5,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x5000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 99,
            },
        ];
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&raw).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(map.usable_bytes(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].end(), 0x3000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].length(), 0x2000);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[0].kind(), RegionKind::Usable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[1].kind(), RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable);
        assert_eq!(map.regions()[2].kind(), RegionKind::Unknown(99));
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_empty_zero_length_overflowing_and_overlapping_maps() {
        assert_eq!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&[]), Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyMap));
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&[RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0,
                length: 0,
                kind: 0
            }]),
            Err(MemoryMapError::EmptyRegion { index: 0 })
        );
        let overflowing = [RawMemoryRegion {
            base: u64::MAX - 3,
            length: 8,
            kind: 0,
        }];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overflowing),
            Err(MemoryMapError::AddressOverflow { index: 0 })
        );

        let overlap = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x2000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2fff,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            MemoryMap::from_raw(&overlap),
            Err(MemoryMapError::OverlappingRegions {
                first: 0,
                second: 1
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn checks_that_a_range_is_contained_in_one_memory_region_kind() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x10000,
                kind: 5,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x20000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        assert!(map.range_is_within_region_kind(0x2000, 0x8000, RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            0x1000,
            0x20000,
            RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable
        ));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_region_kind(0x2000, 0x8000, RegionKind::Usable));
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_acpi_spans_against_region_kinds_and_physical_width() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 2,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 3,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x4000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();

        assert!(map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x2800, Some(16)));
        assert!(map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1000, 0x3000, None));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x4000, None));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1800, 0x2800, Some(12)));
        assert!(!map.range_is_within_acpi_regions(0x1000, 0x1000, None));

        let span = map.validate_acpi_span(0x1800, 0x900, Some(14)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(span.byte_start(), 0x1800);
        assert_eq!(span.byte_end(), 0x2100);
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_start(), 0x1000);
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_end(), 0x3000);
        assert!(span.contains_mapping_page(0x1000));
        assert!(span.contains_mapping_page(0x2000));
        assert!(!span.contains_mapping_page(0x3000));
        assert!(!span.contains_mapping_page(0x1800));
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x2ff0, 0x20, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x1800, 0x900, Some(13)),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(u64::MAX - 15, 16, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_acpi_span(0x1000, 64 * 1024 + 1, None),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::SpanTooLarge)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn validates_legacy_rsdp_only_inside_reserved_firmware_window() {
        let map = MemoryMap::from_raw(&[
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x80_000,
                length: 0x80_000,
                kind: 1,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x10_0000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 2,
            },
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let span = map.validate_rsdp_span(0xf5290, 20, Some(36)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_start(), 0xf5000);
        assert_eq!(span.mapping_end(), 0xf6000);
        assert!(span.contains_mapping_page(0xf5000));
        assert!(!span.contains_mapping_page(0x100000));
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_rsdp_span(0x7fff0, 32, Some(36)),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_rsdp_span(0xffff0, 32, Some(36)),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::NotFullyAcpiBacked)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            map.validate_rsdp_span(0xf5290, 20, Some(19)),
            Err(super::AcpiSpanError::PhysicalRangeOutOfBounds)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_adjacent_ranges_and_rejects_excess_entries() {
        let adjacent = [
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x1000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 0,
            },
            RawMemoryRegion {
                base: 0x2000,
                length: 0x1000,
                kind: 1,
            },
        ];
        assert!(MemoryMap::from_raw(&adjacent).is_ok());

        let mut builder = MemoryMapBuilder::new();
        for index in 0..MAX_MEMORY_REGIONS {
            builder.push((index as u64) * 0x2000, 0x1000, 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            builder.push(0x1_0000_0000, 0x1000, 1),
            Err(MemoryMapError::TooManyRegions)
        );
    }

### Completed in this session

- Limine base revision:
  - `src/boot.rs` makes `BASE_REVISION_REQUEST` writable and volatile-reads its third word before using base-revision-3 guarantees.
  - Important protocol detail, confirmed by official Limine header/docs and QEMU: **zero means supported**; nonzero means unsupported. Do not use `>= 3`.
  - Added `BootInfoError::UnsupportedBaseRevision`.
- Shell/VFS:
  - Added `RamFs::write_file_path` and `append_file_path`, which reject oversized inputs before creating files.

- ACPI:

  - Boot requests RSDP, validates its base revision and physical span, then uses a temporary read-only/NX borrowed page mapping in the cloned page tables to read/copy RSDP → RSDT/XSDT → MADT into `BootInfo`.

  - `CandidatePageTables` supports borrowed ACPI leaf mappings without creating/deallocating `Frame` tokens. Tests cover permission/span checks, duplicate mappings, ownership API mismatch, active guards, release, and frame-exhaustion rollback.
  - Docs and roadmap were updated; Milestone 3 remains explicitly incomplete.
- Validation observed after these changes:
  - `cargo fmt --all` passed.
  - `cargo test --workspace --lib`: **105 passed**.
  - `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-none`: passed.

### Current blocker — QEMU exposed an unhandled hardware-set page-table bit

The last `just smoke` attempt in WSL reached the new temporary ACPI mapping, then halted with:

```text
temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: InvalidIntermediateEntry
```

Likely cause: when the candidate CR3 is temporarily active, hardware sets the **Accessed** bit in intermediate page-table entries. The candidate map/unmap walks currently reject this bit. `src/paging.rs` has two intermediate-entry masks that currently allow only address/present/writable/user:

```rust
let allowed = PTE_ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK | PTE_PRESENT | PTE_WRITABLE | PTE_USER;
```

They occur in map and unmap paths near lines ~2162 and ~2390. Add a `PTE_ACCESSED` constant (`1 << 5`) and allow it in both masks. Then add/adjust host coverage if practical; rerun formatting, tests, target check/build, and QEMU smoke.

Do not simply ignore the unmap error and continue: that would leave a temporary ACPI mapping installed. The current code deliberately halts if it cannot remove the mapping.

## Decisions and constraints

- Read/follow `rustix/AGENTS.md` rules given earlier in the conversation:
  - Kernel remains `no_std`, target `x86_64-unknown-none`.
  - Never dereference arbitrary physical addresses or use the HHDM for ACPI.
  - Only `Usable` ranges become `Frame` tokens.
  - No `sti` before controller routing, IRQ return, EOI, spurious/unexpected policies, and tests are ready.
  - For boot/paging/architecture changes, intended validation is `just verify`.
  - Keep roadmap accurate and do not commit.
- ACPI reader switches CR3 to the complete cloned candidate, copies bytes through one temporary supervisor RO/NX page, restores the inherited CR3 with global TLB flushing, then unmaps while candidate is inactive.
- `read_madt` is host-tested, but the physical mapping/CR3 round-trip is only validated by QEMU.
- ACPI/MMIO/APIC setup, IRQ dispatch, PIT, wait queues, scheduler, and IRQ-driven input are still not implemented. Milestone 3 is **not done**.

    19	- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
    20	- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot, CPUID/address-width reporting, read-only CR0 caching-mode reporting, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT/MTRR reporting.
    21	- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. The opt-in `probe-hhdm-frame` QEMU feature allocates, validates, writes, reads, clears, and returns one `Usable` frame through Limine's HHDM contract. `src/paging.rs` has a bounded candidate-root builder that owns allocator-issued table/leaf tokens and maps/unmaps 4 KiB leaves transactionally. The default boot path clones and activates the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, and retains the active table tokens. A 256 KiB BSS-backed global heap is installed; it has fixed capacity and does not grow from frames.
    22	- Pure 4 KiB mapping-range validation, leaf-PTE bit encoding, PAT layout parsing, and host-tested MTRR/PAT policy in `src/paging.rs`; these helpers check alignment, address widths, canonical virtual ranges, W^X, NXE input, PAT indices, captured-register validity, MTRR overlap rules, and Intel SDM Table 11-7 effective types under normal caching. Discontinuous variable-MTRR masks are explicitly unsupported. A pure selector chooses a PAT index only when its effective type remains uniform across all MTRR boundaries in an aligned physical range, and range-bound selected attributes can encode 4 KiB leaves. The bounded candidate builder stores its unique mutable table-memory backend borrow, uses allocator-issued `Frame` tokens for table pages and leaf mappings, restricts walks to owned tables, and rolls back failures. Active candidates reject mutation and release. Boot captures CR0 caching mode, EFER.NXE, `IA32_PAT`, and a bounded MTRR snapshot read-only when supported, validates the captured state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution.     33	
    34	## Source-of-truth documents
    35	
    36	Consult the relevant documentation before modifying a subsystem:
    37	
    38	- [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) — documentation entry point and current status.
    39	- [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) — milestone sequencing and exit criteria.
    40	- [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) — current architecture and intended layers.
    41	- [`docs/architecture/boot.md`](docs/architecture/boot.md) — Limine requests, boot snapshot, and trust boundary.
    42	- [`docs/architecture/memory.md`](docs/architecture/memory.md) — memory ownership, frame allocator, and paging direction.
    43	- [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) — parser/kernel boundary and shell/VFS contract.
    44	- [`docs/architecture/drivers.md`](docs/architecture/drivers.md) — current driver scope and limitations.
    45	- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — unsafe boundaries and security policy.
    46	- [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) and [`docs/development/testing.md`](docs/development/testing.md) — supported commands and validation expectations.
    47	
    48	When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.
    49	
    50	## Repository map
    51	
    52	- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
    53	- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
    54	- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map, address-width, canonical-address, Limine HHDM-range, and linker-defined kernel segment validation.
    55	- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
    56	- `src/paging.rs` — checked mapping/cache policy, inherited page-table walking, and a bounded candidate-root builder. The default boot path activates a cloned hierarchy and retains its owned table tokens; the HHDM backend accesses only complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames after checked address derivation.
    57	- `src/shell.rs` — serial line editor and kernel-side Crabshell executor.
    58	- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
    59	- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
    60	- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — polling COM1 driver for shell input/output.
    61	- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, assembly stubs, and fatal exception diagnostics.
    62	- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
    63	- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — raw, non-blocking PS/2-compatible scancode polling; not an input subsystem.
    64	- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
    65	- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
    66	- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
    67	- `justfile` — supported development commands.
    68	- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.
    69	
    70	## Engineering rules
    71	
    72	### Keep changes incremental and coherent
    73	
    74	1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
    75	2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
    76	3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
    77	4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
    78	5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
    79	6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.
    80	
    81	### Rust and dependency policy
    82	
    83	- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
    84	- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
    85	- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
    86	- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
    87	- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.
    88	
    89	### Unsafe and hardware code
    90	
    91	Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.
    92	
    93	Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:
    94	
    95	- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
    96	- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
    97	- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
    98	- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
    99	- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. HHDM access is allowed only through checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on the documented Limine contract; never access arbitrary physical addresses. Do not change CR3 until a complete, reviewed transition mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
   100	- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
   101	- The exception setup is fatal-only. It does not enable maskable interrupts, configure a PIC/APIC, or provide recovery. Do not call `sti` or claim interrupt support without an IRQ design and tests.
   102	- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.
   103	
   104	For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.
   105	
   106	### Shell and filesystem contract
   107	
   108	- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
   109	- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
   110	- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
   111	- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
   112	- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.
   113	
   114	## Validation workflow
   115	
   116	Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:
   117	
   118	```sh
   119	just fmt
   120	just test
   121	just check
   122	just build
   123	just image
   124	just smoke
   125	just verify
   126	```
   127	
   128	`just test` runs host-side library tests (memory-map validation, frame allocator, VFS, and Crabshell parser). `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, and QEMU prompt smoke test. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.
   129	
   130	For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.
   131	
   132	Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.
   133	
   134	## Completion criteria for agent changes
   135	
   136	Before reporting work complete:
   137	
   138	- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
   139	- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
   140	- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
   141	- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
   142	- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

     1	//! Host-testable ownership for x86 interrupt vectors reserved for device IRQs.
     2	//!
     3	//! Architectural exceptions occupy vectors 0–31. The upper range 0xf0–0xff is
     4	//! kept unavailable for future local-APIC/spurious vectors; allocated vectors
     5	//! therefore come only from 0x20–0xef. This allocator does not install IDT gates,
     6	//! configure a controller, or enable interrupt delivery.
     7	
     8	pub const FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR: u8 = 0x20;
     9	pub const LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR: u8 = 0xef;
    10	const VECTOR_COUNT: usize = 256;
    11	const VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS: usize = VECTOR_COUNT / u64::BITS as usize;
    12	
    13	/// A vector allocation token. Tokens are not `Copy` or `Clone` and must be
    14	/// returned to the allocator instance that produced them.
    15	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    16	pub struct InterruptVector(u8);
    17	
    18	impl InterruptVector {
    19	    pub const fn number(&self) -> u8 {
    20	        self.0
    21	    }
    22	}
    23	
    24	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    25	pub enum VectorReleaseError {
    26	    ReservedVector,
    27	    NotAllocated,
    28	}
    29	
    30	/// Failure to return a token preserves ownership by returning that token.
    31	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    32	pub struct VectorReleaseFailure {
    33	    pub error: VectorReleaseError,
    34	    pub vector: InterruptVector,
    35	}
    36	
    37	/// Fixed-capacity allocator for vectors 0x20 through 0xef.
    38	///
    39	/// Only one allocator may manage a given CPU's vector namespace. The caller is
    40	/// responsible for keeping it alive while any returned tokens are in use.
    41	pub struct InterruptVectorAllocator {
    42	    allocated: [u64; VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS],
    43	    allocated_count: usize,
    44	}
    45	
    46	impl InterruptVectorAllocator {
    47	    pub const fn new() -> Self {
    48	        let mut allocated = [u64::MAX; VECTOR_BITMAP_WORDS];
    49	        let mut vector = FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR;
    50	        while vector <= LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR {
    51	            let word = vector as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
    52	            let bit = vector as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
    53	            allocated[word] &= !(1u64 << bit);
    54	            vector += 1;
    55	        }
    56	        Self {
    57	            allocated,
    58	            allocated_count: 0,
    59	        }
    60	    }
    61	
    62	    pub fn allocate(&mut self) -> Option<InterruptVector> {
    63	        for number in FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR..=LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR {
    64	            let word = number as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
    65	            let bit = number as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
    66	            let mask = 1u64 << bit;
    67	            if self.allocated[word] & mask == 0 {
    68	                self.allocated[word] |= mask;
    69	                self.allocated_count += 1;
    70	                return Some(InterruptVector(number));
    71	            }
    72	        }
    73	        None
    74	    }
    75	
    76	    pub fn release(&mut self, vector: InterruptVector) -> Result<(), VectorReleaseFailure> {
    77	        if !(FIRST_DEVICE_VECTOR..=LAST_DEVICE_VECTOR).contains(&vector.0) {
    78	            return Err(VectorReleaseFailure {
    79	                error: VectorReleaseError::ReservedVector,
    80	                vector,
    81	            });
    82	        }
    83	        let word = vector.0 as usize / u64::BITS as usize;
    84	        let bit = vector.0 as usize % u64::BITS as usize;
    85	        let mask = 1u64 << bit;
    86	        if self.allocated[word] & mask == 0 {
    87	            return Err(VectorReleaseFailure {
    88	                error: VectorReleaseError::NotAllocated,
    89	                vector,
    90	            });
    91	        }
    92	        self.allocated[word] &= !mask;
    93	        self.allocated_count -= 1;
    94	        Ok(())
    95	    }
    96

```rustix/docs/architecture/interrupts.md
     1	# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation
     2	
     3	## Current implementation
     4	
     5	`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, and IDT gates for architectural exception vectors 0–31. Exceptions are fatal-only. Bootstrap leaves maskable interrupts disabled; there is no PIC/APIC initialization, IRQ entry/dispatch, acknowledgement, or return path.
     6	
     7	`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef`. Exception vectors `0x00..=0x1f` and the upper range `0xf0..=0xff` are reserved. Allocation is bounded and deterministic; releasing an invalid token returns it without changing allocator state. The caller must maintain one allocator per CPU vector namespace and return tokens to their originating allocator.
     8	
     9	The allocator only reserves numbers. It does not install IDT entries or establish that a controller is configured to deliver a vector. Future IRQ registration must couple vector-token ownership with a valid interrupt gate and controller route; sources must remain masked until dispatch and end-of-interrupt handling are ready. Do not enable interrupts as a side effect of installing gates.
    10	
    11	## Required IRQ path
    12	
    13	The initial hardware target remains one-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC setup, legacy PIC masking, IRQ-specific interrupt entry/return, vector ownership, masking/unmasking, EOI, spurious and unexpected IRQ policy, and the PIT tick. A controller route may be unmasked only after its gate, handler, and acknowledgement path are installed and validated. Host tests can check vector and routing policy; QEMU is required for privileged entry, MMIO/port-I/O, delivery, acknowledgement, and timing behavior.
    14	
    15	The fixed kernel heap remains forbidden in IRQ and exception context. Until IRQ-safe synchronization and bounded work are established, handlers must not allocate, block, log via unbounded paths, or take locks that interrupted code can hold.

```

fn page_table_indexes(virtual_address: u64, levels: u8) -> [u16; 5] {
    let mut indexes = [0; 5];
    for (depth, index) in indexes.iter_mut().take(usize::from(levels)).enumerate() {
        let level_number = usize::from(levels) - depth;
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        *index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
    }
    indexes

//! Checked x86_64 mapping policy and a bounded owned page-table builder.
//!
//! Pure helpers validate addresses, permissions, and cache policy. Candidate
//! table access is delegated to an unsafe backend contract. This module never
//! writes CR3; callers may activate a validated hierarchy through the explicit
//! unsafe ownership marker after performing their architecture-specific switch.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind, ValidatedAcpiSpan,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidRootAddress,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
/// Encode a replacement CR3 value while preserving the active low-bit mode.
///
/// PCID is retained but the no-flush bit is always cleared so the selected PCID
/// is invalidated on load. Legacy PWT/PCD controls are preserved unchanged.
pub fn encode_cr3_value(
    root_physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3Error> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    let root_end = root_physical_address
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress)?;
    if root_physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            root_physical_address,
            root_end,
            physical_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress);
    }
    let low = match low_bits {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(pcid) if pcid <= 0x0fff => u64::from(pcid),
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(_) => return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through,
            page_level_cache_disable,
        } => {
            (u64::from(page_level_write_through) << 3) | (u64::from(page_level_cache_disable) << 4)
        }
    };
    Ok(root_physical_address | low)
}

pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,
        error: PageTableEntryError,
    },
    Reader(E),
}

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error>;
}

/// Translate one virtual address by following at most five page-table entries.
///
/// The reader owns all physical-memory access policy. This walker does not turn
/// physical addresses into pointers, modify tables, or infer effective cache
/// types from the leaf PAT selector.
pub fn walk_virtual_address<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    virtual_address: u64,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<PageWalkOutcome, PageWalkError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_address, config.virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress);
    }
    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
    const CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const LARGE_PAGE_PAT: u64 = 1 << 12;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let mut table_physical = root_physical;
    let mut writable = true;
    let mut user_accessible = true;
    let mut executable = true;
    let mut level_number = config.levels;

    loop {
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        let index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
        let entry = reader
            .read_entry(table_physical, index)
            .map_err(PageWalkError::Reader)?;
        let level = match level_number {
            5 => PageLevel::Pml5,
            4 => PageLevel::Pml4,
            3 => PageLevel::Pdpt,
            2 => PageLevel::Pd,
            1 => PageLevel::Pt,
            _ => return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration),
        };
        if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
            return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level });
        }

        let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
        if address_field & !physical_mask != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        if !config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::NxDisabled,
            });
        }
        writable &= entry & WRITABLE != 0;
        user_accessible &= entry & USER != 0;
        executable &= entry & NO_EXECUTE == 0;

        let large_page = level_number > 1 && entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0;
        let leaf_shift = if level_number == 1 {
            12
        } else if large_page && level_number == 2 && config.page_2m_supported {
            21
        } else if large_page && level_number == 3 && config.page_1g_supported {
            30
        } else if large_page && level_number <= 3 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageUnsupported,
            });
        } else if large_page {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
            });
        } else {
            table_physical = address_field;
            level_number -= 1;
            continue;
        };

        if large_page {
            let reserved_alignment_bits = ((1u64 << leaf_shift) - 1) & !0x1fff;
            if entry & reserved_alignment_bits != 0 {
                return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageMisaligned,
                });
            }
        }
        let page_size = 1u64 << leaf_shift;
        let leaf_physical_base = address_field & !(page_size - 1);
        let leaf_physical_end =
            leaf_physical_base
                .checked_add(page_size)
                .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
                })?;
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            leaf_physical_base,
            leaf_physical_end,
            config.physical_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        let pat_bit = if large_page {
            entry & LARGE_PAGE_PAT != 0
        } else {
            entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0
        };
        let pat_index = (u8::from(pat_bit) << 2)
            | (u8::from(entry & CACHE_DISABLE != 0) << 1)
            | u8::from(entry & WRITE_THROUGH != 0);
        return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(PageTranslation {
            physical_address: leaf_physical_base | (virtual_address & (page_size - 1)),
            leaf_physical_base,
            page_size,
            permissions: PagePermissions {
                writable,
                executable,
                user_accessible,
            },
            pat_index,
            raw_leaf_entry: entry,
        }));
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PagePermissions {
    pub writable: bool,
    pub executable: bool,
    pub user_accessible: bool,
}

/// A mapping range whose arithmetic, address widths, alignment, and W^X policy passed validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMappingRange {
    virtual_start: u64,
    virtual_end: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    permissions: PagePermissions,
}

/// PAT selection for one physical extent, derived from supplied PAT/MTRR state.
///
/// This records a uniform effective type across the range, but does not inspect
/// existing mappings or prove that aliases use compatible cache attributes.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SelectedCacheAttributes {
    physical_start: u64,
    physical_end: u64,
    pat_index: u8,
    effective_type: EffectiveMemoryType,
}

impl SelectedCacheAttributes {
    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn pat_index(self) -> u8 {
        self.pat_index
    }

    pub const fn effective_type(self) -> EffectiveMemoryType {
        self.effective_type
    }
}

impl ValidatedMappingRange {
    pub const fn virtual_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_start
    }

    pub const fn virtual_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end
    }

    pub const fn physical_start(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_start
    }

    pub const fn physical_end(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_end
    }

    pub const fn permissions(self) -> PagePermissions {
        self.permissions
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.virtual_end - self.virtual_start
    }

    /// Select PAT attributes that yield one effective type across this range.
    ///
    /// The supplied PAT/MTRR snapshot and `normal_caching` flag must reflect the
    /// active hardware state. This is a policy calculation only; it does not
    /// inspect existing mappings or detect cache-type aliases.
    pub fn select_cache_attributes(
        self,
        policy: CachePolicy,
        pat: PatLayout,
        mtrrs: &ValidatedMtrrLayout,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<SelectedCacheAttributes, MappingError> {
        if self.physical_address_bits != mtrrs.physical_address_bits {
            return Err(MappingError::MtrrPhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        let effective_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack,
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => EffectiveMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => EffectiveMemoryType::WriteCombining,
        };
        let pat_index = mtrrs
            .select_pat_index_for_range(
                self.physical_start,
                self.length(),
                pat,
                effective_type,
                normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(MappingError::CachePolicy)?;

        Ok(SelectedCacheAttributes {
            physical_start: self.physical_start,
            physical_end: self.physical_end,
            pat_index,
            effective_type,
        })
    }

    /// Encode a 4 KiB leaf PTE using attributes selected for this physical range.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry_with_cache_attributes(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        cache_attributes: SelectedCacheAttributes,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if cache_attributes.physical_start != self.physical_start
            || cache_attributes.physical_end != self.physical_end
        {
            return Err(MappingError::CacheAttributesRangeMismatch);
        }
        self.leaf_4k_entry(page_offset, cache_attributes.pat_index, nx_enabled)
    }

    /// Encode a single 4 KiB leaf PTE within this validated range.
    ///
    /// `pat_index` is the raw three-bit PAT index; the caller must have verified
    /// that the active PAT MSR gives it the intended cache semantics. `nx_enabled`
    /// must reflect EFER.NXE, not merely CPUID support. This only creates entry
    /// bits—it neither owns the frame nor writes a page table.
    pub fn leaf_4k_entry(
        self,
        page_offset: u64,
        pat_index: u8,
        nx_enabled: bool,
    ) -> Result<PageTableEntry, MappingError> {
        if page_offset & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(MappingError::UnalignedPageOffset);
        }
        if page_offset >= self.length() {
            return Err(MappingError::PageOffsetOutOfRange);
        }
        if self.physical_address_bits > MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if pat_index > 7 {
            return Err(MappingError::InvalidPatIndex);
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable && !nx_enabled {
            return Err(MappingError::NxNotEnabled);
        }

        let physical_address = self
            .physical_start
            .checked_add(page_offset)
            .ok_or(MappingError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut bits = physical_address | PTE_PRESENT;
        if self.permissions.writable {
            bits |= PTE_WRITABLE;
        }
        if self.permissions.user_accessible {
            bits |= PTE_USER;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b001 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_WRITE_THROUGH;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b010 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_CACHE_DISABLE;
        }
        if pat_index & 0b100 != 0 {
            bits |= PTE_PAT_4K;
        }
        if !self.permissions.executable {
            bits |= PTE_NO_EXECUTE;
        }

        Ok(PageTableEntry(bits))
    }
}

/// Maximum x86_64 physical-address width representable by a 4 KiB PTE.
pub const MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const PTE_PRESENT: u64 = 1 << 0;
const PTE_WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
const PTE_USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
const PTE_WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
const PTE_CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
const PTE_ACCESSED: u64 = 1 << 5;
const PTE_PAT_4K: u64 = 1 << 7;
const PTE_NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;

/// Raw bits for one x86_64 4 KiB leaf page-table entry.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTableEntry(u64);

impl PageTableEntry {
    pub const fn bits(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum CachePolicy {
    WriteBack,
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PatMemoryType {
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
    WriteThrough,
    WriteProtected,
    WriteBack,
    UncacheableMinus,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EffectiveMemoryType {
    Uncacheable,
    WriteCombining,
    WriteThrough,
    WriteProtected,
    WriteBack,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PatLayoutError {
    ReservedBits { index: u8 },
    ReservedMemoryType { index: u8, value: u8 },
}

/// Parsed PAT memory types from an `IA32_PAT` MSR value supplied by the caller.
///
/// Parsing does not read the MSR or establish that this is the active value. The
/// MTRR configuration may also affect the effective cache type for an address.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PatLayout {
    memory_types: [u8; 8],
}

impl PatLayout {
    pub fn from_msr_value(value: u64) -> Result<Self, PatLayoutError> {
        let mut memory_types = [0; 8];
        for (index, memory_type) in memory_types.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let entry = ((value >> (index * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
            if entry & !0x07 != 0 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedBits { index: index as u8 });
            }
            if entry == 0b010 || entry == 0b011 {
                return Err(PatLayoutError::ReservedMemoryType {
                    index: index as u8,
                    value: entry,
                });
            }
            *memory_type = entry;
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    /// Return the first PAT index with the exact requested memory type.
    pub fn index_for(self, policy: CachePolicy) -> Option<u8> {
        let requested_type = match policy {
            CachePolicy::Uncacheable => 0b000,
            CachePolicy::WriteCombining => 0b001,
            CachePolicy::WriteBack => 0b110,
        };
        self.memory_types
            .iter()
            .position(|memory_type| *memory_type == requested_type)
            .map(|index| index as u8)
    }

    fn memory_type_at(self, index: u8) -> Result<PatMemoryType, EffectiveMemoryTypeError> {
        match self.memory_types.get(usize::from(index)).copied() {
            Some(0) => Ok(PatMemoryType::Uncacheable),
            Some(1) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteCombining),
            Some(4) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteThrough),
            Some(5) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteProtected),
            Some(6) => Ok(PatMemoryType::WriteBack),
            Some(7) => Ok(PatMemoryType::UncacheableMinus),
            Some(_) => unreachable!("PAT layouts reject reserved memory types"),
            None => Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::PatIndexOutOfRange { index }),
        }
    }
}

const IA32_MTRRCAP: u32 = 0x0000_00fe;
const IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE: u32 = 0x0000_02ff;
const IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0: u32 = 0x0000_0200;
const MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 8;
const MTRRCAP_PRMRR_SUPPORTED: u64 = 1 << 12; // Recognized but not consumed by this MTRR policy.
const MTRRCAP_KNOWN_BITS: u64 = 0x0dff | MTRRCAP_PRMRR_SUPPORTED;
const FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES: [u32; 11] = [
    0x250, 0x258, 0x259, 0x268, 0x269, 0x26a, 0x26b, 0x26c, 0x26d, 0x26e, 0x26f,
];

/// Maximum variable MTRR pairs retained in the fixed-capacity boot snapshot.
pub const MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS: usize = 32;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisterPair {
    pub base: u64,
    pub mask: u64,
}

/// Raw MTRR state captured for diagnostics; values still require policy validation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrRegisters {
    pub capability: u64,
    pub default_type: u64,
    pub fixed_registers: Option<[u64; 11]>,
    pub variable_register_count: u8,
    pub variable_registers: [MtrrRegisterPair; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrState {
    Unsupported,
    VariableRangeCapacityExceeded { reported_count: u8 },
    Captured(MtrrRegisters),
}

/// Capture a bounded register snapshot using a caller-provided MSR reader.
///
/// This helper performs no hardware access itself. A false support flag returns
/// without invoking the reader; an over-capacity count returns no partial data.
pub fn capture_mtrr_registers(supported: bool, mut read_msr: impl FnMut(u32) -> u64) -> MtrrState {
    if !supported {
        return MtrrState::Unsupported;
    }

    let capability = read_msr(IA32_MTRRCAP);
    let variable_register_count = (capability & 0xff) as u8;
    if usize::from(variable_register_count) > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS {
        return MtrrState::VariableRangeCapacityExceeded {
            reported_count: variable_register_count,
        };
    }

    let default_type = read_msr(IA32_MTRR_DEF_TYPE);
    let fixed_registers = if capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0 {
        let mut registers = [0; FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES.len()];
        for (register, index) in registers.iter_mut().zip(FIXED_MTRR_REGISTER_INDICES) {
            *register = read_msr(index);
        }
        Some(registers)
    } else {
        None
    };

    let mut variable_registers =
        [MtrrRegisterPair { base: 0, mask: 0 }; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
    for (range_index, registers) in variable_registers
        .iter_mut()
        .take(usize::from(variable_register_count))
        .enumerate()
    {
        let base_index = IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE0 + 2 * range_index as u32;
        registers.base = read_msr(base_index);
        registers.mask = read_msr(base_index + 1);
    }

    MtrrState::Captured(MtrrRegisters {
        capability,
        default_type,
        fixed_registers,
        variable_register_count,
        variable_registers,
    })
}

pub const FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT: usize = 88;
const MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS: u8 = 52;
const MTRR_VALID: u64 = 1 << 11;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum MtrrMemoryType {
    Uncacheable = 0,
    WriteCombining = 1,
    WriteThrough = 4,
    WriteProtected = 5,
    WriteBack = 6,
}

impl MtrrMemoryType {
    pub fn from_raw(value: u8) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        match value {
            0 => Ok(Self::Uncacheable),
            1 => Ok(Self::WriteCombining),
            4 => Ok(Self::WriteThrough),
            5 => Ok(Self::WriteProtected),
            6 => Ok(Self::WriteBack),
            value => Err(MtrrError::ReservedMemoryType { value }),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MtrrError {
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    ReservedCapabilityBits,
    ReservedDefaultTypeBits,
    ReservedBaseBits,
    ReservedMaskBits,
    UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask,
    MisalignedVariableBase,
    InvalidVariableRange,
    ReservedMemoryType { value: u8 },
    FixedRangesUnavailable,
    FixedRegisterSupportMismatch,
    VariableRegisterCountMismatch,
    WriteCombiningUnsupported,
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch,
    UndefinedOverlap,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EffectiveMemoryTypeError {
    Mtrr(MtrrError),
    PatIndexOutOfRange { index: u8 },
    NonNormalCachingMode,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NoUniformPatIndex { requested: EffectiveMemoryType },
}

/// Decoded fixed MTRR memory types in ascending physical-address order.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FixedMtrrRanges {
    memory_types: [MtrrMemoryType; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT],
}

impl FixedMtrrRanges {
    /// Decode FIX64K_00000, FIX16K_80000/A0000, and FIX4K_C0000..F8000.
    pub fn from_msr_values(registers: [u64; 11]) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        let mut memory_types = [MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable; FIXED_MTRR_TYPE_COUNT];
        for (register_index, value) in registers.iter().enumerate() {
            for slot in 0..8 {
                let memory_type = ((value >> (slot * 8)) & 0xff) as u8;
                memory_types[register_index * 8 + slot] = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(memory_type)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { memory_types })
    }

    fn type_for_address(&self, address: u64) -> Option<MtrrMemoryType> {
        let index = if address < 0x80_000 {
            (address / 0x1_0000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xa0_000 {
            8 + ((address - 0x80_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0xc0_000 {
            16 + ((address - 0xa0_000) / 0x4000) as usize
        } else if address < 0x10_0000 {
            24 + ((address - 0xc0_000) / 0x1000) as usize
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        Some(self.memory_types[index])
    }
}

/// One supported variable-range MTRR with a power-of-two mask and aligned base.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VariableMtrr {
    base_match: u64,
    address_mask: u64,
    range_start: u64,
    range_end: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    memory_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    enabled: bool,
}

impl VariableMtrr {
    /// Decode one IA32_MTRR_PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK pair. A clear valid bit returns `Ok(None)`.
    /// Discontinuous masks permitted by some CPUs are explicitly unsupported.
    pub fn from_msr_values(
        base: u64,
        mask: u64,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
        if base & !(physical_mask | 0xff) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedBaseBits);
        }
        if mask & !(physical_mask | MTRR_VALID) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedMaskBits);
        }
        let memory_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((base & 0xff) as u8)?;
        if mask & MTRR_VALID == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }

        let address_mask = mask & physical_mask;
        let ignored_page_bits = (physical_mask ^ address_mask) >> 12;
        if ignored_page_bits & ignored_page_bits.wrapping_add(1) != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::UnsupportedDiscontinuousVariableMask);
        }
        let ignored_address_bits = physical_mask ^ address_mask;
        if base & ignored_address_bits != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::MisalignedVariableBase);
        }

        let range_start = base & address_mask;
        let range_size = ignored_address_bits + PAGE_SIZE;
        let range_end = range_start
            .checked_add(range_size)
            .filter(|end| *end <= (1u64 << physical_address_bits))
            .ok_or(MtrrError::InvalidVariableRange)?;

        Ok(Some(Self {
            base_match: range_start,
            address_mask,
            range_start,
            range_end,
            physical_address_bits,
            memory_type,
            enabled: true,
        }))
    }

    const fn inactive(physical_address_bits: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            base_match: 0,
            address_mask: 0,
            range_start: 0,
            range_end: 0,
            physical_address_bits,
            memory_type: MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable,
            enabled: false,
        }
    }

    fn matches(self, address: u64) -> bool {
        self.enabled && address & self.address_mask == self.base_match
    }
}

/// MTRR policy decoded from supplied register values; it does not access MSRs.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MtrrLayout<'a> {
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    enabled: bool,
    fixed_enabled: bool,
    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
    variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
}

impl<'a> MtrrLayout<'a> {
    pub fn new(
        physical_address_bits: u8,
        enabled: bool,
        fixed_enabled: bool,
        default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
        fixed_ranges: Option<&'a FixedMtrrRanges>,
        variable_ranges: &'a [VariableMtrr],
    ) -> Result<Self, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if enabled && fixed_enabled && fixed_ranges.is_none() {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
        }
        if variable_ranges
            .iter()
            .any(|range| range.physical_address_bits != physical_address_bits)
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressWidthMismatch);
        }

        Ok(Self {
            physical_address_bits,
            enabled,
            fixed_enabled,
            default_type,
            fixed_ranges,
            variable_ranges,
        })
    }

    fn next_boundary_after(&self, address: u64, end: u64) -> u64 {
        if !self.enabled {
            return end;
        }

        let mut next = end;
        if self.fixed_enabled {
            if let Some(boundary) = next_fixed_mtrr_boundary(address) {
                if boundary < next {
                    next = boundary;
                }
            }
        }
        for range in self.variable_ranges.iter().filter(|range| range.enabled) {
            for boundary in [range.range_start, range.range_end] {
                if boundary > address && boundary < next {
                    next = boundary;
                }
            }
        }
        next
    }

    /// Resolve the MTRR type for one physical address, rejecting undefined overlaps.
    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
        if address >= (1u64 << self.physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange);
        }
        if !self.enabled {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if self.fixed_enabled {
            if let Some(memory_type) = self
                .fixed_ranges
                .and_then(|ranges| ranges.type_for_address(address))
            {
                return Ok(memory_type);
            }
        }

        let mut matched_types = 0u8;
        for range in self.variable_ranges {
            if range.matches(address) {
                matched_types |= 1 << range.memory_type as u8;
            }
        }
        if matched_types == 0 {
            return Ok(self.default_type);
        }
        if matched_types & (1 << MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable as u8) != 0 {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::Uncacheable);
        }
        if matched_types.count_ones() == 1 {
            return MtrrMemoryType::from_raw(matched_types.trailing_zeros() as u8);
        }
        let write_back_and_through =
            (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteBack as u8) | (1 << MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough as u8);
        if matched_types == write_back_and_through {
            return Ok(MtrrMemoryType::WriteThrough);
        }
        Err(MtrrError::UndefinedOverlap)
    }
}

fn next_fixed_mtrr_boundary(address: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    match address {
        0..0x80_000 => Some((address / 0x1_0000 + 1) * 0x1_0000),
        0x80_000..0xa0_000 => Some(0x80_000 + ((address - 0x80_000) / 0x4000 + 1) * 0x4000),
        0xa0_000..0xc0_000 => Some(0xa0_000 + ((address - 0xa0_000) / 0x4000 + 1) * 0x4000),
        0xc0_000..0x10_0000 => Some(0xc0_000 + ((address - 0xc0_000) / 0x1000 + 1) * 0x1000),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Fully decoded MTRR state. Construction rejects malformed or incomplete
/// captured register snapshots before they can influence a mapping policy.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ValidatedMtrrLayout {
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    enabled: bool,
    fixed_enabled: bool,
    default_type: MtrrMemoryType,
    fixed_ranges: Option<FixedMtrrRanges>,
    variable_ranges: [VariableMtrr; MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS],
}

impl MtrrRegisters {
    pub fn validated_layout(
        &self,
        physical_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<ValidatedMtrrLayout, MtrrError> {
        if !(12..=MAX_MTRR_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(MtrrError::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
        }
        if self.capability & !MTRRCAP_KNOWN_BITS != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedCapabilityBits);
        }
        if self.default_type & !0x0cff != 0 {
            return Err(MtrrError::ReservedDefaultTypeBits);
        }

        let reported_count = (self.capability & 0xff) as usize;
        if reported_count > MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS
            || reported_count != usize::from(self.variable_register_count)
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::VariableRegisterCountMismatch);
        }

        let fixed_supported = self.capability & MTRRCAP_FIXED_SUPPORTED != 0;
        if fixed_supported != self.fixed_registers.is_some() {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRegisterSupportMismatch);
        }
        let enabled = self.default_type & MTRR_ENABLED != 0;
        let fixed_enabled = self.default_type & MTRR_FIXED_ENABLED != 0;
        if fixed_enabled && !fixed_supported {
            return Err(MtrrError::FixedRangesUnavailable);
        }

        let default_type = MtrrMemoryType::from_raw((self.default_type & 0xff) as u8)?;
        let write_combining_supported = self.capability & MTRRCAP_WRITE_COMBINING_SUPPORTED != 0;
        if default_type == MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining && !write_combining_supported {
            return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
        }

        let fixed_ranges = self
            .fixed_registers
            .map(FixedMtrrRanges::from_msr_values)
            .transpose()?;
        if fixed_ranges.as_ref().is_some_and(|ranges| {
            ranges
                .memory_types
                .contains(&MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining)
        }) && !write_combining_supported
        {
            return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
        }

        let mut variable_ranges =
            [VariableMtrr::inactive(physical_address_bits); MAX_CAPTURED_VARIABLE_MTRRS];
        for (index, pair) in self
            .variable_registers
            .iter()
            .take(reported_count)
            .enumerate()
        {
            if let Some(range) =
                VariableMtrr::from_msr_values(pair.base, pair.mask, physical_address_bits)?
            {
                if range.memory_type == MtrrMemoryType::WriteCombining && !write_combining_supported
                {
                    return Err(MtrrError::WriteCombiningUnsupported);
                }
                variable_ranges[index] = range;
            }
        }

        Ok(ValidatedMtrrLayout {
            physical_address_bits,
            enabled,
            fixed_enabled,
            default_type,
            fixed_ranges,
            variable_ranges,
        })
    }
}

impl ValidatedMtrrLayout {
    fn as_layout(&self) -> MtrrLayout<'_> {
        MtrrLayout {
            physical_address_bits: self.physical_address_bits,
            enabled: self.enabled,
            fixed_enabled: self.fixed_enabled,
            default_type: self.default_type,
            fixed_ranges: self.fixed_ranges.as_ref(),
            variable_ranges: &self.variable_ranges,
        }
    }

    pub fn memory_type_for(&self, address: u64) -> Result<MtrrMemoryType, MtrrError> {
        self.as_layout().memory_type_for(address)
    }

    /// Resolve the Intel SDM PAT/MTRR table for one address and PAT index.
    /// `normal_caching` must reflect CR0.CD=0 and CR0.NW=0.
    pub fn effective_memory_type_for(
        &self,
        address: u64,
        pat: PatLayout,
        pat_index: u8,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<EffectiveMemoryType, EffectiveMemoryTypeError> {
        if !normal_caching {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode);
        }
        let mtrr_type = self
            .memory_type_for(address)
            .map_err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr)?;
        let pat_type = pat.memory_type_at(pat_index)?;
        Ok(combine_mtrr_pat_types(mtrr_type, pat_type))
    }

    /// Select the lowest PAT index that yields one effective type across an
    /// aligned physical range. This checks MTRR transition boundaries, not aliases.
    pub fn select_pat_index_for_range(
        &self,
        physical_start: u64,
        length: u64,
        pat: PatLayout,
        requested: EffectiveMemoryType,
        normal_caching: bool,
    ) -> Result<u8, EffectiveMemoryTypeError> {
        if !normal_caching {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::NonNormalCachingMode);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (physical_start | length) & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let end = physical_start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if end > (1u64 << self.physical_address_bits) {
            return Err(EffectiveMemoryTypeError::Mtrr(
                MtrrError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            ));
        }

        let layout = self.as_layout();
        let mut candidates = u8::MAX;
        let mut address = physical_start;
        while address < end {
            let mtrr_type = layout
